summary.zh: 人口增长 + 价格上涨 + enclosure → 农民生活恶化、城市贫民增加;传统节庆(Carnival)与社区惩罚(charivari)延续,但新教与天主教改革都试图规训大众文化。
summary.en: Population growth + rising prices + enclosure → peasants worse off and more urban poor; traditional festivals (Carnival) and community shaming rituals (charivari) persisted, but both Protestant and Catholic reformers tried to discipline popular culture.

detail.zh: 社会等级仍是 hierarchy:贵族、教士、市民、农民。商业精英开始用财富买地、买官进入贵族。惩罚公开进行:颈手枷(pillory/stocks)、鞭刑、烙印;斗熊等 blood sports 流行。
detail.en: Society remained hierarchical: nobles, clergy, townspeople, peasants. Wealthy merchants bought land and offices to join the nobility. Punishment was public: the pillory and stocks, whipping, branding; blood sports such as bear-baiting were popular.

summary.zh: Mannerism:打破文艺复兴的平衡与和谐,用拉长的人体、扭曲的空间、强烈情感表现宗教动荡时代的不安 —— El Greco、晚期 Michelangelo。
summary.en: Mannerism: broke Renaissance balance and harmony with elongated figures, distorted space, and intense emotion, expressing the anxiety of an age of religious upheaval — El Greco, late Michelangelo.

detail.zh: El Greco 的《The Burial of the Count of Orgaz》是经典例子。Tintoretto 的戏剧化光线与构图也属此风格。
detail.en: El Greco’s The Burial of the Count of Orgaz is a classic example. Tintoretto’s dramatic light and composition belong to the same style.

summary.zh: 天主教改革需要打动信众情感 → Baroque:宏大、戏剧性光影、运动感;Bernini(St. Peter’s 广场)、Caravaggio(明暗对比)、Rubens;也被绝对君主用来炫耀权力(Versailles)。
summary.en: The Catholic Reformation wanted art that stirred emotion → the Baroque: grandeur, dramatic light, and motion; Bernini (St. Peter’s Square), Caravaggio (chiaroscuro), Rubens; absolutist monarchs also used it to display power (Versailles).

detail.zh: 对比:新教荷兰的艺术(Rembrandt、Vermeer)偏向朴素的日常生活和商人肖像,反映不同的赞助人和宗教文化。女画家 Artemisia Gentileschi 以强烈明暗和女性主角闻名。
detail.en: Contrast: Protestant Dutch art (Rembrandt, Vermeer) favored everyday scenes and merchant portraits, reflecting different patrons and religious culture. Artemisia Gentileschi became famous for dramatic chiaroscuro and powerful female subjects.

summary.zh: James I 宣扬 divine right of kings;Charles I 未经议会同意征税 → 议会通过 Petition of Right(1628)→ Charles 解散议会、独自统治 11 年。
summary.en: James I preached the divine right of kings; Charles I levied taxes without Parliament → Parliament passed the Petition of Right (1628) → Charles dissolved Parliament and ruled alone for 11 years.

detail.zh: Charles 和大主教 Laud 推行接近天主教的礼仪,激怒 Puritans;强迫苏格兰使用英国祈祷书 → 苏格兰起义 → 被迫召开议会(1640)。
detail.en: Charles and Archbishop Laud imposed near-Catholic ritual, angering Puritans; forcing the English prayer book on Scotland → Scottish revolt → Charles had to recall Parliament (1640).

summary.zh: Royalists（Cavaliers）与 Parliamentarians（Roundheads）交战；Oliver Cromwell 的 New Model Army 获胜。Charles I 于 1649 年受审并被处决，显示议会派对君主权威的激烈挑战。
summary.en: Royalists (Cavaliers) fought Parliamentarians (Roundheads); Oliver Cromwell’s New Model Army won. Charles I was tried and executed in 1649, marking a radical challenge to royal authority.

detail.zh: 内战中出现激进派:Levellers(主张扩大选举权)、Diggers(主张土地公有)。
detail.en: Radicals emerged: the Levellers (wider male suffrage) and the Diggers (common ownership of land).

summary.zh: 英国成为共和国,但很快变成 Cromwell 的军事独裁(Lord Protector)、严格清教道德 → 他死后,议会复辟君主制,迎回 Charles II(1660)。
summary.en: England became a republic but soon a military dictatorship under Cromwell as Lord Protector, with strict Puritan morality → after his death Parliament restored the monarchy under Charles II (1660).

detail.zh: Cromwell 残酷镇压 Ireland。Hobbes《Leviathan》(1651)在内战背景下主张强大的绝对主权以避免"所有人对所有人的战争"。
detail.en: Cromwell brutally subdued Ireland. Hobbes’s Leviathan (1651), written amid civil war, argued for an absolute sovereign to prevent a "war of all against all."

summary.zh: 天主教徒 James II 生下天主教继承人 → 议会邀请 William & Mary(新教)入主 → James 逃亡,几乎不流血 → English Bill of Rights(1689):国王不得未经议会征税、维持常备军、中止法律。
summary.en: Catholic James II fathered a Catholic heir → Parliament invited Protestant William and Mary → James fled with almost no bloodshed → the English Bill of Rights (1689): no taxes, standing army, or suspension of laws without Parliament.

detail.zh: 同年 Toleration Act 给予非国教新教徒宗教自由(不含天主教徒)。John Locke《Two Treatises of Government》为其辩护:政府基于被统治者同意,保护生命、自由、财产。
detail.en: The Toleration Act (1689) granted freedom of worship to Protestant dissenters (not Catholics). John Locke’s Two Treatises justified it: government rests on consent and protects life, liberty, and property.

summary.zh: 议会主权确立;Hanover 王朝(1714)的国王不太管政事 → Robert Walpole 成为事实上的第一位首相,内阁制度形成 —— 但选举权仍只属于少数有产者。
summary.en: Parliamentary sovereignty was established; the Hanoverian kings (1714) left politics to ministers → Robert Walpole became the first de facto prime minister and cabinet government took shape — yet only a small propertied elite could vote.

detail.zh: 变化:王权受法律和议会约束;延续:贵族与 gentry 仍主导政治,直到 19 世纪改革法案(Unit 6)。
detail.en: Change: the crown was bound by law and Parliament; continuity: aristocrats and gentry still ran politics until the 19th-century Reform Acts (Unit 6).

summary.zh: 荷兰人和英国人先行:crop rotation(芜菁、苜蓿代替休耕)、Jethro Tull 的 seed drill、Townshend 的四轮作、选育牲畜 → 粮产增加 → 人口增长。
summary.en: The Dutch and English led: crop rotation (turnips and clover replacing fallow), Jethro Tull’s seed drill, Charles "Turnip" Townshend’s four-field system, selective breeding → more food → population growth.

detail.zh: 美洲作物(土豆、玉米)也提高热量供应。农业革命是工业革命的前提(Unit 6)。
detail.en: American crops (potatoes, maize) also added calories. The Agricultural Revolution set the stage for industrialization (Unit 6).

summary.zh: 地主用围栏把公共土地(commons)私有化,搞大规模商业农业 → 效率提高,但小农失去土地 → 成为雇工或进城,为工业提供劳动力。
summary.en: Landlords fenced in the common lands for large-scale commercial farming → higher efficiency, but small farmers lost access → they became wage laborers or moved to towns, supplying labor for industry.

detail.zh: 英国议会通过大量 Enclosure Acts。东欧则相反:农奴制加强(second serfdom),贵族用农奴劳动为西欧市场生产粮食。
detail.en: Parliament passed many Enclosure Acts. Eastern Europe went the other way: serfdom intensified (the "second serfdom") as nobles used serf labor to grow grain for Western markets.

summary.zh: 商人把原料(羊毛、棉花)发给农村家庭纺纱织布,再收回成品 → 绕开城市行会、利用农闲劳力 —— proto-industrialization。
summary.en: Merchants delivered raw materials (wool, cotton) to rural households to spin and weave, then collected the goods → bypassed urban guilds and used seasonal labor — proto-industrialization.

detail.zh: 变化:生产走向市场与资本主义;延续:仍在家里用手工工具,家庭(包括妇女儿童)一起劳动。18 世纪后期纺织机械(spinning jenny、water frame、spinning mule)开始把生产推向工厂(Unit 6)。
detail.en: Change: production became market-oriented and capitalist; continuity: work stayed at home with hand tools, involving the whole family including women and children. Late-18th-century textile machines (the spinning jenny, water frame, spinning mule) began moving production into factories (Unit 6).

summary.zh: 国家财富 = 金银储备 → 追求贸易顺差:高关税、补贴本国工业、建设道路运河、建立殖民地 —— 法国财政大臣 Jean-Baptiste Colbert 是典型。
summary.en: National wealth = bullion → pursue a favorable balance of trade: tariffs, subsidies for domestic industry, roads and canals, colonies — exemplified by France’s finance minister Jean-Baptiste Colbert.

detail.zh: 英国的 Navigation Acts(1651 起)规定殖民地贸易必须用英国船,打击荷兰,引发英荷战争。
detail.en: England’s Navigation Acts (from 1651) required colonial trade to use English ships, targeting the Dutch and sparking the Anglo-Dutch Wars.

summary.zh: 荷兰共和国:VOC、Bank of Amsterdam、Amsterdam stock exchange、庞大商船队 → 欧洲最富;政治上是共和制、宗教上相对宽容(吸引犹太人、Huguenots)。
summary.en: The Dutch Republic: the VOC, the Bank of Amsterdam, the Amsterdam stock exchange, and a huge merchant fleet → Europe’s richest society; politically a republic, religiously tolerant (welcoming Jews and Huguenots).

detail.zh: 商人阶层赞助艺术:Rembrandt、Vermeer 画市民生活与团体肖像。18 世纪因英法竞争和战争而相对衰落。Tulip mania(1637)是早期金融泡沫。Joint-stock company 和有限责任(limited liability)让投资者分散风险。
detail.en: Merchants patronized art: Rembrandt and Vermeer painted burghers and group portraits. The Dutch declined relatively in the 18th century amid English and French competition and war. Tulip mania (1637) was an early speculative bubble. Joint-stock companies with limited liability let investors spread their risk.

summary.zh: "L’état, c’est moi":Versailles 把贵族圈在宫廷礼仪中、远离地方权力;intendants 代表国王管理各省;从不召开 Estates-General;废除 Edict of Nantes(1685)。
summary.en: "L’état, c’est moi": Versailles trapped nobles in court ritual away from local power; royal intendants ran the provinces; he never called the Estates-General; he revoked the Edict of Nantes (1685).

detail.zh: Fronde(1648–1653)贵族叛乱让少年 Louis 决心驯服贵族。废除 Edict of Nantes 导致约 20 万 Huguenots 出逃,带走技术和资本。Bishop Bossuet 为君权神授辩护。Louis 年幼时由 Cardinal Mazarin 主政;他削弱了 Parlements(高等法院)审查王令的权力。
detail.en: The Fronde (1648–1653) noble revolt convinced the young Louis to tame the nobility. Revoking the Edict of Nantes drove out about 200,000 Huguenots and their skills. Bishop Bossuet defended divine right. Cardinal Mazarin governed during Louis’s minority; Louis curbed the Parlements’ power to challenge royal edicts.

summary.zh: 强制西化:学习西欧造船与军事、剃胡子、建St. Petersburg("window on the West");Table of Ranks:贵族地位取决于为国服务;把东正教会置于国家控制下(Holy Synod)。
summary.en: Forced Westernization: Western shipbuilding and military methods, shaved beards, a new capital at St. Petersburg ("window on the West"); the Table of Ranks tied noble status to state service; the Orthodox Church was put under state control (the Holy Synod).

detail.zh: Great Northern War 击败瑞典,获得波罗的海出海口。改革主要惠及精英,农奴制反而加强。年轻时微服出访西欧(Grand Embassy)学习造船;打压旧贵族 boyars;建立 Russian Academy of Sciences。
detail.en: The Great Northern War defeated Sweden and won a Baltic outlet. Reforms served the elite; serfdom actually deepened. As a young tsar he toured Western Europe in disguise (the Grand Embassy) to learn shipbuilding; he broke the old boyar nobility and founded the Russian Academy of Sciences.

summary.zh: Great Elector Frederick William 建立常备军和税收 → Frederick William I("Soldier King")把国家变成"有国家的军队";Junkers(地主贵族)担任军官,换取对农奴的控制。
summary.en: The Great Elector Frederick William built a standing army and taxes → Frederick William I (the "Soldier King") made Prussia "an army with a state"; the Junkers (landed nobles) served as officers in exchange for control over their serfs.

detail.zh: 普鲁士小而分散,用纪律、效率的官僚和军队弥补资源不足。Frederick the Great 的开明专制见 Unit 4。
detail.en: Small and scattered, Prussia made up for limited resources with a disciplined army and efficient bureaucracy. Frederick the Great’s enlightened absolutism is in Unit 4.

summary.zh: 1683 年击退 Ottoman 围攻 Vienna → 收复 Hungary;但帝国多民族、多语言,只能与各地贵族妥协,集权程度不及法、普;Pragmatic Sanction 保证女儿 Maria Theresa 继位。
summary.en: Repelled the Ottoman siege of Vienna (1683) → regained Hungary; but the empire was multiethnic and multilingual, so rulers had to bargain with regional nobles and centralized less than France or Prussia; the Pragmatic Sanction secured Maria Theresa’s succession.

detail.zh: Maria Theresa 继位引发 War of the Austrian Succession(1740),普鲁士夺走 Silesia。
detail.en: Her accession triggered the War of the Austrian Succession (1740), in which Prussia seized Silesia.

summary.zh: 贵族选举国王、议会 liberum veto(任何一位议员可否决)→ 中央极弱 → 被俄、普、奥三次瓜分(1772、1793、1795),从地图上消失。
summary.en: Nobles elected the king, and the liberum veto let any single deputy block legislation → a powerless center → partitioned three times by Russia, Prussia, and Austria (1772, 1793, 1795) and erased from the map.

detail.zh: 反面案例:说明在 balance of power 体系里,不能集权的国家会被邻国吞并。议会称 Sejm;末代国王 Stanisław II。
detail.en: The counterexample: in a balance-of-power system, a state that could not centralize was devoured by its neighbors. Its parliament was the Sejm; the last king was Stanisław II.

summary.zh: Louis XIV 想把法国边界推到"自然疆界"(莱茵河)→ 多次战争(War of Devolution、Dutch War、Nine Years’ War)→ William of Orange 组织反法联盟 → 法国扩张受阻。
summary.en: Louis XIV sought "natural frontiers" at the Rhine → repeated wars (War of Devolution, Dutch War, Nine Years’ War) → William of Orange organized anti-French coalitions → French expansion was checked.

detail.zh: 战争耗尽法国财政,为 18 世纪法国的财政危机埋下伏笔(Unit 5)。
detail.en: The wars drained French finances, foreshadowing the 18th-century fiscal crisis (Unit 5).

summary.zh: Louis XIV 的孙子 Philip 继承西班牙王位 → 欧洲担心法西合并 → 大联盟开战 → Peace of Utrecht(1713):Philip V 保住西班牙但法西永不合并;英国获得 Gibraltar、asiento(奴隶贸易特许)和北美领土。
summary.en: Louis XIV’s grandson Philip inherited Spain → Europe feared a Franco-Spanish union → a Grand Alliance went to war → the Peace of Utrecht (1713): Philip V kept Spain but the crowns could never unite; Britain gained Gibraltar, the asiento, and North American lands.

detail.zh: Utrecht 是 balance of power 原则的典型体现;英国开始成为海上与殖民霸主。
detail.en: Utrecht is the textbook expression of the balance of power; Britain emerged as the leading naval and colonial power.

summary.zh: Frederick the Great 趁 Maria Theresa 继位之机夺取富庶的 Silesia → 普鲁士跃升为大国,与奥地利长期对抗(德意志二元争霸)。
summary.en: Frederick the Great exploited Maria Theresa’s accession to seize wealthy Silesia → Prussia became a great power and Austria’s lasting rival (German dualism).

detail.zh: 这场冲突在北美称为 King George’s War,体现欧洲战争的全球化。
detail.en: In North America it was King George’s War — evidence that European wars were going global.

summary.zh: Diplomatic Revolution(1756):奥地利与宿敌法国结盟,英国与普鲁士结盟 → 全球战争(欧洲、北美、印度)→ Treaty of Paris(1763):英国获得 Canada 和印度优势,法国失去大部分北美帝国。
summary.en: The Diplomatic Revolution (1756): Austria allied with old enemy France, Britain with Prussia → a global war (Europe, North America, India) → the Treaty of Paris (1763): Britain gained Canada and dominance in India; France lost most of its North American empire.

detail.zh: 战争债务让英国向北美殖民地征税(→ 美国革命),也加重法国财政危机(→ 法国大革命)。普鲁士保住 Silesia。
detail.en: War debts led Britain to tax its American colonies (→ the American Revolution) and deepened France’s fiscal crisis (→ the French Revolution). Prussia kept Silesia.

summary.zh: Nicolaus Copernicus《On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres》提出日心说(heliocentric),挑战 Ptolemy 的地心说 —— 但仍保留圆形轨道。
summary.en: Nicolaus Copernicus’s On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres proposed a heliocentric universe, challenging Ptolemy’s geocentric model — though he kept circular orbits.

detail.zh: 《On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres》于 1543 年、Copernicus 生命末期出版。同年 Vesalius 出版《On the Fabric of the Human Body》，用解剖纠正 Galen；更早的 Paracelsus 用化学药物挑战 Galen 的体液医学。
detail.en: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres was published in 1543, near the end of Copernicus’s life. That year Vesalius published On the Fabric of the Human Body, using dissection to challenge Galen. Earlier, Paracelsus challenged Galen’s humoral medicine with chemical remedies.

summary.zh: Tycho Brahe 积累了大量精确观测数据 → 助手 Johannes Kepler 用数学证明行星轨道是椭圆(三大行星运动定律)。
summary.en: Tycho Brahe gathered massive precise observations → his assistant Johannes Kepler used mathematics to show planetary orbits are ellipses (three laws of planetary motion).

detail.zh: 体现科学方法:观测数据 + 数学推理。
detail.en: A model of the new method: observational data + mathematical reasoning.

summary.zh: Galileo 用望远镜观察到木星卫星、月球环形山,支持日心说;研究惯性和自由落体 → 1633 年被宗教裁判所审判,被迫放弃日心说、软禁终身。
summary.en: Galileo used the telescope to see Jupiter’s moons and lunar craters, supporting heliocentrism; he studied inertia and falling bodies → in 1633 the Inquisition tried him, forced him to recant, and confined him for life.

detail.zh: 《Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems》用意大利文写作,面向大众。Galileo 案成为科学与宗教冲突的象征。
detail.en: His Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems was written in Italian for a wide audience. His trial became the symbol of conflict between science and religion.

summary.zh: Francis Bacon:empiricism / inductive 推理 —— 从观察和实验出发得出结论;René Descartes:rationalism / deductive 推理 —— "I think, therefore I am",数学与怀疑一切。
summary.en: Francis Bacon: empiricism and inductive reasoning — reason from observation and experiment; René Descartes: rationalism and deductive reasoning — "I think, therefore I am," mathematics and systematic doubt.

detail.zh: 二者结合 = 科学方法。Descartes 的 mind-body dualism 影响深远;他还发明解析几何。
detail.en: Combined, they form the scientific method. Descartes’s mind–body dualism was hugely influential; he also invented analytic geometry.

summary.zh: Isaac Newton《Principia》:万有引力与三大运动定律,用同一套数学法则解释天上和地上的运动 → 宇宙像一台可被理性理解的机器 → 启发启蒙运动用理性寻找社会的"自然法则"。
summary.en: Isaac Newton’s Principia: universal gravitation and three laws of motion explained heavenly and earthly motion with one set of mathematical laws → a machine-like universe knowable by reason → inspired the Enlightenment to seek natural laws of society.

detail.zh: Newton 本人很虔诚,但他的宇宙观为 deism(钟表匠上帝)铺路。其他:Harvey(血液循环)、Boyle(气体定律)。
detail.en: Newton was devout, but his cosmos paved the way for deism (the clockmaker God). Others: Harvey (circulation of blood), Boyle (gas law).

summary.zh: 国家支持科学:英国 Royal Society(1660)、法国 Academy of Sciences(1666)→ 科学成为有组织的公共事业,学术期刊分享发现。
summary.en: States sponsored science: England’s Royal Society (1660) and France’s Academy of Sciences (1666) → science became an organized public enterprise with journals to share findings.

detail.zh: 女性多被排除在学院之外,但仍有贡献:Margaret Cavendish、Maria Winkelmann(天文学)。延续:炼金术、占星术等传统思想与新科学并存很久(Newton 也研究炼金术)。
detail.en: Women were mostly excluded, yet contributed: Margaret Cavendish, Maria Winkelmann (astronomy). Continuity: alchemy and astrology coexisted with the new science for a long time (Newton studied alchemy too).

summary.zh: Two Treatises of Government:人有生命、自由、财产的自然权利,政府基于被统治者同意,违约可被推翻;Essay Concerning Human Understanding:心灵是 tabula rasa,知识来自经验。
summary.en: Two Treatises of Government: natural rights to life, liberty, and property; government rests on consent of the governed and may be overthrown if it violates them; Essay Concerning Human Understanding: the mind is a tabula rasa shaped by experience.

detail.zh: Tabula rasa 意味着教育和环境可以改造人 → 启蒙改革乐观主义的基础。Locke 直接影响了美国《独立宣言》。
detail.en: Tabula rasa meant education and environment could improve people — the root of Enlightenment optimism. Locke directly shaped the Declaration of Independence.

summary.zh: 《The Spirit of the Laws》:三权分立与制衡(立法、行政、司法)防止专制,以英国为榜样。
summary.en: The Spirit of the Laws: separation of powers and checks and balances (legislative, executive, judicial) to prevent despotism, with England as a model.

detail.zh: Persian Letters 用外国人视角讽刺法国社会。对美国宪法影响巨大。
detail.en: His Persian Letters satirized French society through foreign eyes. Hugely influential on the U.S. Constitution.

summary.zh: Voltaire:批判宗教狂热与教会("Écrasez l’infâme")、主张宗教宽容与言论自由;deism;《Candide》讽刺盲目乐观。
summary.en: Voltaire: attacked religious fanaticism and the Church ("Écrasez l’infâme"), championed religious toleration and free speech; a deist; Candide mocked naive optimism.

detail.zh: 为 Calas 案(新教徒被冤杀)奔走。支持开明专制,曾在 Frederick the Great 宫廷。
detail.en: He campaigned in the Calas affair (a Protestant wrongly executed). He favored enlightened monarchy and spent time at Frederick the Great’s court.

summary.zh: 《The Social Contract》:主权属于人民的 general will,"人生而自由,却无处不在枷锁之中";《Emile》:儿童教育应顺应天性 —— 但认为女性应从属于男性、在家庭中服务。
summary.en: The Social Contract: sovereignty lies in the people’s general will — "Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains"; Emile: education should follow a child’s nature — yet he held women should be subordinate and domestic.

detail.zh: Rousseau 重视情感,是启蒙中的"异类",影响了浪漫主义(Unit 5)和法国大革命的激进派(Robespierre)。
detail.en: Rousseau valued feeling, an outlier among the philosophes who influenced Romanticism (Unit 5) and radical revolutionaries such as Robespierre.

summary.zh: Denis Diderot 主编《Encyclopédie》:汇集科学、技术、哲学知识,暗含对教会和专制的批评 → 启蒙思想的"总纲",多次被禁仍广泛流传。
summary.en: Denis Diderot edited the Encyclopédie: a compendium of science, technology, and philosophy laced with criticism of Church and crown → the Enlightenment’s summary statement, banned repeatedly yet widely read.

detail.zh: 启蒙传播网络:salons(由 Madame Geoffrin 等女性主持)、咖啡馆、阅读会、Masonic lodges、Republic of Letters 书信网络 → 形成 public sphere(公共领域)。
detail.en: Diffusion network: salons hosted by women such as Madame Geoffrin, coffeehouses, reading societies, Masonic lodges, and the Republic of Letters → the emergence of a public sphere.

summary.zh: Cesare Beccaria《On Crimes and Punishments》:反对酷刑和死刑,刑罚应与罪行相称;Adam Smith《The Wealth of Nations》:laissez-faire、"invisible hand",批判重商主义;Physiocrats(Quesnay):土地是财富之源。
summary.en: Cesare Beccaria’s On Crimes and Punishments: against torture and the death penalty, punishment proportional to crime; Adam Smith’s The Wealth of Nations: laissez-faire and the "invisible hand," a critique of mercantilism; the Physiocrats (Quesnay): land is the source of wealth.

detail.zh: Smith 主张分工提高生产力;这些思想为 19 世纪自由主义经济学奠基(Unit 6)。法国财政大臣 Turgot 尝试按 Physiocrat 思想取消行会与粮食管制,被特权阶层赶下台。
detail.en: Smith argued division of labor raised productivity; his ideas founded 19th-century liberal economics (Unit 6). French minister Turgot tried Physiocratic reforms — abolishing guilds and grain controls — and was ousted by the privileged.

summary.zh: Mary Wollstonecraft《A Vindication of the Rights of Woman》:把启蒙的理性与平等原则用到女性身上,要求女子教育 —— 回应 Rousseau 的女性观。
summary.en: Mary Wollstonecraft’s A Vindication of the Rights of Woman: applied Enlightenment reason and equality to women and demanded education for women — a direct answer to Rousseau.

detail.zh: Olympe de Gouges《Declaration of the Rights of Woman》(1791,Unit 5)。多数 philosophes 并没有把平等延伸到女性。
detail.en: Olympe de Gouges’s Declaration of the Rights of Woman (1791, Unit 5). Most philosophes did not extend equality to women.

summary.zh: Deism:上帝像钟表匠,创造宇宙后不再干预;David Hume 的怀疑论;但同时出现宗教复兴:英国 Methodism(John Wesley)、德意志 Pietism —— 强调情感和个人信仰。
summary.en: Deism: God as a clockmaker who built the universe and no longer intervenes; David Hume’s skepticism; yet also religious revival: English Methodism (John Wesley) and German Pietism stressed emotion and personal faith.

detail.zh: C/C 考点:启蒙运动让精英世俗化,但大众宗教热情依然强烈。更激进的 Baron d’Holbach 主张无神论(atheism)与唯物主义;Condorcet 相信人类无限进步。
detail.en: Continuity/change point: elites grew more secular, but popular religious fervor remained strong. The more radical Baron d’Holbach argued for atheism and materialism; Condorcet believed in limitless human progress.

summary.zh: 瘟疫消退(最后一次大鼠疫约 1720 Marseille)+ 农业革命与土豆增加粮食 + 交通改善缓解饥荒 → 死亡率下降 → 欧洲人口快速增长。
summary.en: Plague receded (the last major outbreak, Marseille c. 1720) + the Agricultural Revolution and the potato added food + better transport eased famine → death rates fell → rapid population growth.

detail.zh: 医学本身贡献有限(除了天花接种,Jenner 1796 牛痘疫苗)。人口增长为工业革命提供劳动力和市场。Lady Mary Wortley Montagu 把奥斯曼的天花接种法带回英国。
detail.en: Medicine helped little apart from smallpox inoculation (Jenner’s cowpox vaccine, 1796). Growth supplied labor and markets for industrialization. Lady Mary Wortley Montagu brought Ottoman smallpox inoculation to Britain.

summary.zh: 西北欧晚婚、核心家庭;受 Locke、Rousseau 影响,中上层开始把童年看作需要关爱与教育的阶段,出现 companionate marriage(基于感情的婚姻)。
summary.en: Northwestern Europe kept late marriage and nuclear families; influenced by Locke and Rousseau, middle and upper classes began to treat childhood as a stage needing affection and education, and companionate marriage spread.

detail.zh: 延续:下层家庭仍需要孩子劳动,弃婴(foundling hospitals)和高婴儿死亡率依然普遍。
detail.en: Continuity: poor families still relied on children’s labor, and infant abandonment (foundling hospitals) and high infant mortality persisted.

summary.zh: 殖民地商品(糖、咖啡、茶、烟草)与便宜棉布、陶瓷普及 → 中产甚至下层也成为消费者;咖啡馆成为讨论政治与商业的公共空间。
summary.en: Colonial goods (sugar, coffee, tea, tobacco) and cheaper cottons and ceramics spread → middle and even lower classes became consumers; coffeehouses became public spaces for politics and business.

detail.zh: Josiah Wedgwood 的陶瓷营销是例子。"Industrious revolution":家庭更努力工作以购买新商品。
detail.en: Josiah Wedgwood’s pottery marketing is a classic example. The "industrious revolution": households worked harder to afford new goods.

summary.zh: 识字率上升(尤其新教地区)→ 报纸、期刊、小说、廉价 chapbooks 大量出现 → 形成 public sphere(公众舆论),新思想能挑战权威。
summary.en: Rising literacy (especially in Protestant areas) → newspapers, journals, novels, and cheap chapbooks multiplied → a public sphere of public opinion that could challenge authority.

detail.zh: 小说兴起(Richardson、Defoe)。Jürgen Habermas 的 public sphere 概念常被用来解释这一现象。其他小说家:Henry Fielding、Jane Austen;流通图书馆(lending libraries)让中产也能读书。
detail.en: The novel rose (Richardson, Defoe). Habermas’s concept of the public sphere is often used to explain it. Other novelists: Henry Fielding, Jane Austen; lending libraries put books within middle-class reach.

summary.zh: Rococo:轻盈、华丽、贵族享乐(Fragonard、Watteau);Neoclassicism:模仿古希腊罗马,强调秩序、公民美德(Jacques-Louis David《Oath of the Horatii》);音乐:Bach、Handel(Baroque),Mozart、Haydn(Classical)。
summary.en: Rococo: light, ornate, aristocratic pleasure (Fragonard, Watteau); Neoclassicism: imitated Greece and Rome, stressing order and civic virtue (Jacques-Louis David’s Oath of the Horatii); music: Bach and Handel (Baroque), Mozart and Haydn (Classical).

detail.zh: Neoclassicism 与启蒙、法国大革命的共和理想相连;Rococo 被批评为贵族腐化的象征。
detail.en: Neoclassicism tied into Enlightenment and revolutionary republican ideals; Rococo was criticized as a symbol of aristocratic decadence.

summary.zh: 自称"国家的第一仆人";宗教宽容、废除大部分酷刑、法律改革、推广土豆与教育;与 Voltaire 通信 —— 但保留农奴制、依靠 Junkers。
summary.en: Called himself "the first servant of the state"; religious toleration, abolition of most torture, legal reform, promotion of potatoes and schooling; corresponded with Voltaire — but kept serfdom and relied on the Junkers.

detail.zh: 他也是战争君主:夺取 Silesia,参与第一次瓜分 Poland。
detail.en: He was also a war king: he seized Silesia and joined the first partition of Poland.

summary.zh: Maria Theresa 加强中央、改革税收与教育;Joseph II 最激进:Edict of Toleration(1781)、废除农奴制、关闭修道院 → 贵族与教会强烈反对 → 死后很多改革被撤销。
summary.en: Maria Theresa centralized and reformed taxes and schooling; Joseph II went furthest: the Edict of Toleration (1781), abolished serfdom, closed monasteries → fierce noble and Church resistance → many reforms were reversed after his death.

detail.zh: Joseph II 的失败说明:没有贵族支持,自上而下的激进改革难以持久。
detail.en: Joseph II’s failure shows that radical reform from above could not last without noble support.

summary.zh: 与 Voltaire、Diderot 通信,召开立法委员会(Nakaz);但 Pugachev Rebellion(1773–1775)后加强农奴制,用 Charter of the Nobility(1785)换取贵族支持;扩张领土(黑海、瓜分 Poland)。
summary.en: She corresponded with Voltaire and Diderot and called a Legislative Commission (the Nakaz); but after the Pugachev Rebellion (1773–1775) she tightened serfdom and won noble loyalty with the Charter of the Nobility (1785); she expanded to the Black Sea and partitioned Poland.

detail.zh: Catherine 是"开明"与"专制"矛盾的最清楚例子。
detail.en: Catherine is the clearest case of the tension between "enlightened" and "absolutist."

summary.zh: 开明专制的共同局限:不放弃绝对权力、不解放农奴(Joseph II 除外)、改革为国家实力服务;对比:英国是议会制,法国 Louis XV/XVI 改革失败,Poland 被瓜分。
summary.en: Common limits: no surrender of absolute power, no emancipation of serfs (except Joseph II), reforms serving state power; contrast: Britain’s parliamentary rule, France’s failed reforms under Louis XV and XVI, and partitioned Poland.

detail.zh: 犹太人地位:部分君主有限解禁(Joseph II),但普遍仍受限制;Moses Mendelssohn 推动犹太启蒙(Haskalah)。
detail.en: Jews: some rulers granted limited rights (Joseph II), but restrictions remained widespread; Moses Mendelssohn led the Jewish Enlightenment (Haskalah).

summary.zh: 三角贸易与种植园经济(糖、烟草、棉花、咖啡)→ 港口城市(Liverpool、Bristol、Nantes、Bordeaux)致富 → 商业资本积累,欧洲消费习惯改变。
summary.en: The triangular trade and plantation economy (sugar, tobacco, cotton, coffee) → port cities (Liverpool, Bristol, Nantes, Bordeaux) grew rich → commercial capital accumulated and European consumption changed.

detail.zh: Saint-Domingue(今 Haiti)是全世界最赚钱的殖民地,依靠数十万被奴役的非洲人。
detail.en: Saint-Domingue (today’s Haiti) was the world’s most profitable colony, worked by hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans.

summary.zh: Bank of England(1694)+ 议会担保的国债 → 英国可以低息大量借款打仗;法国没有议会信用、税制混乱 → 借款利息高、财政脆弱。
summary.en: The Bank of England (1694) + national debt backed by Parliament → Britain could borrow cheaply and heavily for war; France lacked parliamentary credit and had a chaotic tax system → expensive loans and fragile finances.

detail.zh: South Sea Bubble(1720)与法国 John Law 的 Mississippi Bubble 都是投机泡沫;英国恢复更快。
detail.en: The South Sea Bubble (1720) and John Law’s Mississippi Bubble in France were speculative crashes; Britain recovered faster.

summary.zh: 皇家海军保护贸易 + 殖民地扩张 → Treaty of Paris (1763) 得 Canada、印度优势 → 英国成为全球霸主;失去 13 殖民地(1783)后转向印度与亚洲。
summary.en: The Royal Navy protected trade + colonial expansion → the Treaty of Paris (1763) brought Canada and dominance in India → Britain became the leading global power; after losing the 13 colonies (1783) it turned to India and Asia.

detail.zh: 英国东印度公司在 Plassey(1757)击败孟加拉,开始统治印度。
detail.en: The British East India Company’s victory at Plassey (1757) began British rule in India.

summary.zh: 法国为报复英国资助美国革命 → 法国债务暴增 → 财政危机;同时美国证明启蒙原则(同意、自然权利)可以建国 → 鼓舞欧洲。
summary.en: France financed the American Revolution to avenge itself on Britain → French debt soared → fiscal crisis; meanwhile America showed that Enlightenment principles (consent, natural rights) could found a state → inspiring Europeans.

detail.zh: Lafayette 等法国军官回国后传播革命理念。
detail.en: French officers such as Lafayette returned home carrying revolutionary ideas.

summary.zh: 三个等级:First Estate(教士)、Second Estate(贵族)几乎免税,Third Estate(97% 人口)承担赋税 + 国家破产 + 1788 年歉收面包涨价 + 启蒙思想 → 革命。
summary.en: Three estates: the First (clergy) and Second (nobility) were largely tax-exempt while the Third Estate (97% of people) bore the taxes + state bankruptcy + the 1788 harvest failure and bread prices + Enlightenment ideas → revolution.

detail.zh: Calonne 等财政大臣想向特权等级征税,被 Assembly of Notables 拒绝 → Louis XVI 被迫召开 175 年来首次 Estates-General。
detail.en: Finance ministers such as Calonne tried to tax the privileged and were refused by the Assembly of Notables → Louis XVI had to call the first Estates-General in 175 years.

summary.zh: 争议:按等级投票还是按人头投票 → 第三等级自称 National Assembly → Tennis Court Oath:不制定宪法不解散。Abbé Sieyès《What Is the Third Estate?》。
summary.en: Dispute: voting by order or by head → the Third Estate declared itself the National Assembly → the Tennis Court Oath: no dissolution until a constitution was written. Abbé Sieyès’s What Is the Third Estate?

detail.zh: 按等级投票时，每个等级一票；如果第一与第二等级联合投票，就能以 2:1 压过第三等级。优势取决于两者投票一致，并非算术上“永远”自动如此。
detail.en: Under voting by order, each estate had one vote; if the First and Second Estates voted together, they could outvote the Third Estate two to one. That advantage depended on their voting together rather than being an automatic outcome.

summary.zh: 7 月 14 日巴黎民众攻占 Bastille → 农村 Great Fear 烧毁领主契约 → 8 月 4 日废除封建特权 → 8 月 26 日 Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen:人生而自由平等、主权在民。
summary.en: July 14: Parisians stormed the Bastille → the rural Great Fear burned manorial records → August 4: feudal privileges abolished → August 26: the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen — men are born free and equal, sovereignty resides in the nation.

detail.zh: Declaration 受 Locke、Rousseau、美国《独立宣言》影响。10 月 women’s march on Versailles 把王室押回巴黎。
detail.en: The Declaration drew on Locke, Rousseau, and the American Declaration. In October the women’s march on Versailles brought the royal family back to Paris.

title.zh: Civil Constitution of the Clergy & Constitution of 1791
title.en: Civil Constitution of the Clergy & Constitution of 1791

summary.zh: 没收教会土地;Civil Constitution of the Clergy 让教士成为国家雇员、须宣誓效忠 → 分裂了天主教农民与革命;1791 宪法建立君主立宪,只有纳税的"active citizens"有选举权。
summary.en: Church lands were seized; the Civil Constitution of the Clergy made priests state employees who had to swear loyalty → it split Catholic peasants from the Revolution; the 1791 Constitution created a constitutional monarchy with voting limited to tax-paying "active citizens."

detail.zh: Louis XVI 出逃 Varennes(1791)被抓回,君主信誉崩溃。Olympe de Gouges《Declaration of the Rights of Woman》要求女性平等。
detail.en: Louis XVI’s flight to Varennes (1791) failed and destroyed trust in the king. Olympe de Gouges’s Declaration of the Rights of Woman demanded equality for women.

summary.zh: 对奥普开战 + Brunswick Manifesto 威胁巴黎 → sans-culottes 攻入王宫 → National Convention 宣布共和国(1792 年 9 月)→ 1793 年 1 月处决 Louis XVI。
summary.en: War with Austria and Prussia + the Brunswick Manifesto threatening Paris → the sans-culottes stormed the palace → the National Convention declared a republic (September 1792) → Louis XVI was executed in January 1793.

detail.zh: Convention 中 Jacobins 分为 Girondins(较温和、外省)与 Montagnards(激进、巴黎)。
detail.en: Within the Convention, the Jacobins split into the Girondins (moderate, provincial) and the Montagnards (radical, Parisian).

summary.zh: 外有战争、内有 Vendée 叛乱和通胀 → Robespierre 与 Committee of Public Safety 实行恐怖:约 1.7 万人被正式处决(断头台);levée en masse 全民征兵;最高限价;dechristianization、革命历法。
summary.en: Foreign war, the Vendée revolt, and inflation → Robespierre and the Committee of Public Safety ran the Terror: about 17,000 official executions (the guillotine); the levée en masse mobilized the nation; price controls (the Maximum); dechristianization and a revolutionary calendar.

detail.zh: Robespierre 用 Rousseau 的"美德与恐怖"辩护。Levée en masse 创造了第一支现代全民军队。Jacobin 领袖还有 Danton(后被处决)和 Marat(被刺杀);王后 Marie Antoinette 1793 年被处决。
detail.en: Robespierre justified it as "virtue and terror," echoing Rousseau. The levée en masse created the first modern mass army. Other Jacobin leaders included Danton (later guillotined) and Marat (assassinated); Queen Marie Antoinette was executed in 1793.

summary.zh: Thermidorian Reaction(1794 年 7 月):Robespierre 被处决 → Directory(五人执政)代表有产资产阶级,腐败无能、左右夹击 → 1799 年 Napoleon 发动政变(Brumaire)。
summary.en: The Thermidorian Reaction (July 1794): Robespierre was executed → the Directory (five directors) represented propertied bourgeois, corrupt and squeezed from left and right → Napoleon’s coup of Brumaire (1799).

detail.zh: 革命回到"中间":放弃恐怖与价格管制,但不恢复君主制。
detail.en: The Revolution swung back to the center: it ended the Terror and price controls but did not restore the monarchy.

summary.zh: Saint-Domingue 被奴役者受"自由平等"鼓舞起义,Toussaint L’Ouverture 领导 → 法国 1794 年废奴 → 击败 Napoleon 远征军 → 1804 年 Haiti 独立:第一个由前奴隶建立的国家。
summary.en: Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue, inspired by liberty and equality, rose under Toussaint L’Ouverture → France abolished slavery in 1794 → Napoleon’s expedition was defeated → Haiti became independent in 1804, the first state founded by formerly enslaved people.

detail.zh: Napoleon 1802 年在其他法属殖民地恢复奴隶制。Haiti 的失败让 Napoleon 放弃美洲,1803 年出售 Louisiana。
detail.en: Napoleon restored slavery in other French colonies in 1802. Losing Haiti led him to abandon the Americas and sell Louisiana in 1803.

summary.zh: Edmund Burke《Reflections on the Revolution in France》(1790):批评抽象权利,主张渐进与传统 → conservatism 的起点;Thomas Paine《Rights of Man》为革命辩护;各国君主镇压激进派。
summary.en: Edmund Burke’s Reflections on the Revolution in France (1790) attacked abstract rights and defended gradual change and tradition → the birth of conservatism; Thomas Paine’s Rights of Man defended the Revolution; monarchs repressed radicals.

detail.zh: 法国革命把欧洲政治分成左(革命、共和)与右(保守、君主)—— 这对词本身就来自国民议会座位。
detail.en: The Revolution divided European politics into left (revolution, republic) and right (conservatism, monarchy) — terms born from the seating of the National Assembly.

summary.zh: 意大利、埃及战役成名 → 1799 Brumaire 政变 成为 First Consul → 用公民投票(plebiscite)合法化 → 1804 年自己加冕为皇帝。
summary.en: Fame from campaigns in Italy and Egypt → the coup of Brumaire (1799) made him First Consul → plebiscites lent legitimacy → in 1804 he crowned himself emperor.

detail.zh: 他声称结束革命的混乱,用"秩序"换取"自由"。
detail.en: He promised to end revolutionary chaos, trading liberty for order.

summary.zh: 保留:Napoleonic (Civil) Code——法律面前平等、财产权、废除封建特权,careers open to talent;背离:审查新闻、秘密警察、女性和儿童在法律上从属于男性家长;Concordat of 1801 与教皇和解。
summary.en: Kept: the Napoleonic (Civil) Code — legal equality, property rights, no feudal privilege, careers open to talent; betrayed: press censorship, secret police, women and children legally subordinate to the male head of household; the Concordat of 1801 reconciled with the pope.

detail.zh: 经典 C/C:Napoleon 巩固了革命的社会成果,却废除了政治自由。还建立了 Bank of France 和 lycées(公立中学)。
detail.en: A classic continuity/change item: Napoleon secured the Revolution’s social gains while abolishing political freedom. He also founded the Bank of France and the lycées.

summary.zh: Austerlitz(1805)、Jena(1806)击败奥普俄 → 解散 HRE、建立 Confederation of the Rhine → 在征服地推行 Civil Code、废除封建制;但 Trafalgar(1805)海战败给英国 → Continental System 封锁英国贸易。
summary.en: Victories at Austerlitz (1805) and Jena (1806) → he dissolved the HRE and created the Confederation of the Rhine → imposed the Civil Code and ended feudalism in conquered lands; but defeat at Trafalgar (1805) by Britain → the Continental System to blockade British trade.

detail.zh: Continental System 损害欧洲大陆经济,走私猖獗,最终因俄国退出而崩溃。
detail.en: The Continental System hurt continental economies, encouraged smuggling, and collapsed when Russia withdrew.

summary.zh: 民族主义反抗:Peninsular War(西班牙游击战);1812 年入侵俄国失败(焦土 + 冬季,60 万大军仅剩约 10 万)→ Leipzig(1813)→ 流放 Elba → Hundred Days → Waterloo(1815)→ 流放 St. Helena。
summary.en: Nationalist resistance: the Peninsular War (Spanish guerrillas); the 1812 invasion of Russia failed (scorched earth + winter; of roughly 600,000 men, perhaps 100,000 returned) → Leipzig (1813) → exile to Elba → the Hundred Days → Waterloo (1815) → exile to St. Helena.

detail.zh: 讽刺:Napoleon 传播的民族与平等观念,反过来成了被征服民族反抗他的武器(Fichte《Addresses to the German Nation》)。
detail.en: Irony: the ideas of nation and equality he spread became weapons against him (Fichte’s Addresses to the German Nation).

summary.zh: 奥地利首相 Metternich 主导 → legitimacy:Bourbon 复辟(Louis XVIII);balance of power:法国周围建缓冲带(Netherlands 合并、Prussia 得 Rhineland、Piedmont 加强);法国未被严惩,被纳入新秩序。
summary.en: Austrian minister Metternich led → legitimacy: the Bourbons restored (Louis XVIII); balance of power: buffers around France (a united Netherlands, Prussia on the Rhine, a stronger Piedmont); France was not harshly punished and was brought into the new order.

detail.zh: 参与者:Metternich(奥)、Castlereagh(英)、Alexander I(俄)、Hardenberg(普)、Talleyrand(法)。German Confederation 取代 HRE。维也纳体系维持了大国间约一个世纪无全面战争。
detail.en: Participants: Metternich, Castlereagh, Alexander I, Hardenberg, Talleyrand. The German Confederation replaced the HRE. The settlement kept the great powers from general war for about a century.

summary.zh: Quadruple Alliance(奥、普、俄、英)定期开会维持秩序 = Concert of Europe;Holy Alliance(奥、普、俄)以宗教名义镇压革命 —— 保守主义成为官方政策(详见 Unit 6)。
summary.en: The Quadruple Alliance (Austria, Prussia, Russia, Britain) met regularly to keep order = the Concert of Europe; the Holy Alliance (Austria, Prussia, Russia) pledged in religious terms to suppress revolution — conservatism as official policy (see Unit 6).

detail.zh: 对比 1919 年 Versailles:维也纳把战败国纳入体系,Versailles 惩罚德国 —— LEQ 常考对比。
detail.en: Compare Versailles in 1919: Vienna included the defeated power, while Versailles punished Germany — a common LEQ comparison.

summary.zh: 对启蒙理性和工业化的反弹:强调情感、直觉、想象、自然之美、中世纪与民族历史、个人天才 → 与民族主义紧密相连。
summary.en: A reaction against Enlightenment reason and industrialization: it prized emotion, intuition, and imagination, the beauty of nature, the medieval and national past, and individual genius → closely tied to nationalism.

detail.zh: Rousseau 是先驱;Herder 的 Volksgeist(民族精神)、Grimm 兄弟收集民间故事,都把文化与民族联系起来。
detail.en: Rousseau was a forerunner; Herder’s Volksgeist and the Brothers Grimm’s folk tales linked culture to the nation.

summary.zh: 文学:Wordsworth(自然)、Byron(为希腊独立而死)、Goethe、Victor Hugo;绘画:Delacroix《Liberty Leading the People》、Caspar David Friedrich(崇高自然)、Turner;音乐:Beethoven、Chopin。
summary.en: Literature: Wordsworth (nature), Byron (died for Greek independence), Goethe, Victor Hugo; painting: Delacroix’s Liberty Leading the People, Caspar David Friedrich (sublime nature), Turner; music: Beethoven, Chopin.

detail.zh: Mary Shelley《Frankenstein》(1818)表达对科学与理性越界的忧虑。宗教复兴(Chateaubriand《Genius of Christianity》)也是浪漫主义的一部分。
detail.en: Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818) voiced fears of science overreaching. Religious revival (Chateaubriand’s Genius of Christianity) was also part of Romanticism.

summary.zh: 煤和铁储量丰富且靠近 + 资本(贸易、殖民、银行)+ 劳动力(人口增长、圈地)+ 市场(殖民地、国内)+ 稳定的议会政府与产权保护 + 河流运河港口 → 工业革命首先在英国发生。
summary.en: Abundant, nearby coal and iron + capital (trade, empire, banking) + labor (population growth, enclosure) + markets (colonies and home) + a stable parliamentary government protecting property + rivers, canals, ports → industrialization began in Britain.

detail.zh: 英国没有内部关税、行会力量弱;非国教新教徒被排除在公职之外,转而经商创业。
detail.en: Britain had no internal tariffs and weak guilds; Protestant dissenters, barred from public office, turned to business.

summary.zh: 纺织业先机械化:flying shuttle(Kay)、spinning jenny(Hargreaves)、water frame(Arkwright,工厂制度)→ James Watt 改良蒸汽机(1769)→ 工厂离开河边 → Stephenson 的 Rocket,Liverpool–Manchester Railway(1830)。
summary.en: Textiles mechanized first: the flying shuttle (Kay), spinning jenny (Hargreaves), water frame (Arkwright, the factory system) → James Watt’s improved steam engine (1769) → factories freed from rivers → Stephenson’s Rocket and the Liverpool–Manchester Railway (1830).

detail.zh: 棉花来自美国南方奴隶劳动(Eli Whitney 轧棉机)。Crystal Palace 万国博览会(1851)展示英国工业领先。
detail.en: Raw cotton came from enslaved labor in the American South (Whitney’s cotton gin). The Great Exhibition at the Crystal Palace (1851) displayed British industrial leadership.

summary.zh: 欧陆追赶:Belgium 最快(煤铁);政府主导建铁路、关税保护;Zollverein(1834,普鲁士关税同盟);Friedrich List 主张保护幼稚产业;投资银行(Crédit Mobilier)。
summary.en: The continent caught up: Belgium first (coal and iron); governments led with railways and protective tariffs; the Zollverein (1834, Prussian customs union); Friedrich List urged protecting infant industries; investment banks (Crédit Mobilier).

detail.zh: 东欧和南欧工业化慢:农奴制(俄国到 1861)、缺资本、交通差 → 东西欧差距扩大。List 的《National System of Political Economy》主张 protectionism。
detail.en: Eastern and southern Europe lagged: serfdom (Russia until 1861), little capital, poor transport → a widening East–West gap. List’s National System of Political Economy argued for protectionism.

summary.zh: 1861 年农奴解放后,财政大臣 Sergei Witte 用外国贷款、关税保护和国家投资修建 Trans-Siberian Railway → 1890 年代俄国工业快速增长;Peter Stolypin(1906 起)改革土地、扶植富农。
summary.en: After the 1861 emancipation, finance minister Sergei Witte used foreign loans, protective tariffs, and state investment to build the Trans-Siberian Railway → rapid industrial growth in the 1890s; Peter Stolypin (from 1906) reformed land tenure to build a class of prosperous peasants.

detail.zh: 工业化集中在少数城市,形成新的工人阶级,却没有政治改革 → 为 1905、1917 年革命埋下伏笔(Unit 8)。
detail.en: Industry clustered in a few cities and created a new working class without political reform — setting up the revolutions of 1905 and 1917 (Unit 8).

summary.zh: 新产业:钢(Bessemer 炼钢法)、化工、电力、内燃机、石油 → 德国和美国超越英国;大企业、cartels(德国)和流水线;通信:电报、电话、无线电。
summary.en: New industries: steel (the Bessemer process), chemicals, electricity, the internal combustion engine, oil → Germany and the U.S. overtook Britain; big business, cartels (Germany), assembly lines; communication by telegraph, telephone, radio.

detail.zh: 变化:科学与工业结合(研究实验室);延续:英国仍是金融和航运中心。消费社会出现:百货公司、广告。德国 Krupp 家族的钢铁与军火帝国;冷藏火车车厢、邮购目录、大规模生产(mass production)改变消费。
detail.en: Change: science fused with industry (research labs); continuity: Britain remained the center of finance and shipping. Consumer society emerged: department stores and advertising. Germany’s Krupp family built a steel and arms empire; refrigerated railcars, mail-order catalogs, and mass production changed consumption.

summary.zh: 土豆枯萎病 → Irish Potato Famine(1845–1849)约 100 万人死亡、100 万人移民 → 英国废除 Corn Laws(1846),转向自由贸易。
summary.en: Potato blight → the Irish Potato Famine (1845–1849): about 1 million dead and 1 million emigrants → Britain repealed the Corn Laws (1846) and turned to free trade.

detail.zh: Corn Laws 保护地主的粮价;Anti-Corn Law League(Cobden、Bright)代表工业资本家要求廉价粮食。
detail.en: The Corn Laws protected landowners’ grain prices; the Anti-Corn Law League (Cobden, Bright) spoke for industrialists wanting cheap food.

summary.zh: 人口涌入工业城市(Manchester)→ 拥挤贫民窟、污水、霍乱爆发 → Edwin Chadwick 的报告 → 英国 Public Health Act(1848)、下水道与供水建设。
summary.en: People poured into industrial cities (Manchester) → crowded slums, sewage, cholera outbreaks → Edwin Chadwick’s report → Britain’s Public Health Act (1848) and new sewers and water supply.

detail.zh: Haussmann 重建 Paris(1850s–1860s):宽阔林荫大道、下水道,也便于镇压起义。Pasteur 的细菌理论推动卫生改革。工人挤在 tenements(廉租公寓);有轨电车(streetcars)让中产搬到郊区(suburbs)。
detail.en: Haussmann rebuilt Paris (1850s–1860s) with wide boulevards and sewers — also making barricades harder. Pasteur’s germ theory spurred sanitation. Workers crowded into tenements; streetcars let the middle class move to the suburbs.

summary.zh: 工作与家庭分离 → 中产阶级separate spheres:男人在公共领域工作,女人在家庭("cult of domesticity"、"angel in the house");工人阶级女性和儿童仍需进工厂。
summary.en: Work separated from home → the middle-class ideal of separate spheres: men in the public world of work, women in the home (the "cult of domesticity," the "angel in the house"); working-class women and children still had to labor in factories.

detail.zh: 中产阶级以勤劳、节制、体面(respectability)自我定义。出生率在 19 世纪后期开始下降。
detail.en: The middle class defined itself by hard work, thrift, and respectability. Birth rates began to fall in the late 19th century.

summary.zh: 议会调查（Sadler Report）揭露童工处境；Factory Act（1833）限制纺织厂童工工时并禁止雇用 9 岁以下儿童；Mines Act（1842）禁止女性、女孩及 10 岁以下男孩在地下矿井工作；Ten Hours Act（1847）进一步限制妇女与青少年工时。
summary.en: Parliamentary inquiries such as the Sadler Report exposed child labor. The Factory Act (1833) limited children’s hours in textile mills and prohibited employment under age 9; the Mines Act (1842) prohibited underground mine work by women, girls, and boys under 10; the Ten Hours Act (1847) further limited women’s and young persons’ hours.

detail.zh: 改革来自人道主义者、宗教团体和部分托利党贵族,而不是自由放任的工厂主。
detail.en: Reform came from humanitarians, religious groups, and some Tory aristocrats rather than laissez-faire mill owners.

summary.zh: Luddites(1811–1816)捣毁机器;Chartism(1838–1848)用 People’s Charter 要求成年男子普选、秘密投票、议员领薪;19 世纪后期合法工会和劳工政党(英国 Labour Party 1900、德国 SPD)。
summary.en: Luddites (1811–1816) smashed machines; Chartism (1838–1848) petitioned with the People’s Charter for universal male suffrage, the secret ballot, and paid MPs; by the late 1800s legal unions and labor parties (Britain’s Labour Party 1900, Germany’s SPD).

detail.zh: Chartism 当时失败,但大部分诉求后来都实现了。Combination Acts(1799)曾禁止工会,1824 年废除。
detail.en: Chartism failed at the time, but most of its demands were later enacted. The Combination Acts (1799) had banned unions until their repeal in 1824.

summary.zh: Reform Act 1832:取消 rotten boroughs、给中产阶级选举权;1867(Disraeli):城市工人男性;1884:农村男性 —— 英国通过渐进改革避免了革命。
summary.en: The Reform Act of 1832 abolished rotten boroughs and enfranchised the middle class; 1867 (Disraeli) added urban working men; 1884 added rural men — gradual reform let Britain avoid revolution.

detail.zh: 英国 1918 年给予年满 30 岁且符合相关财产资格等条件的部分女性议会选举权；1928 年女性获得与男性相同年龄条件的选举权。英国另在 1829 年通过 Catholic Emancipation，1833 年通过帝国废奴立法。
detail.en: In Britain, the 1918 act enfranchised some women aged 30 and above who met the relevant property and other qualifications; in 1928 women gained voting rights on the same age terms as men. Britain also passed Catholic Emancipation in 1829 and imperial slavery-abolition legislation in 1833.

summary.zh: Bismarck 为削弱社会主义推出社会保险(医疗 1883、工伤 1884、养老 1889)→ 欧洲福利国家的开端;英国 Liberal 政府的养老金与国民保险(1906–1911);专业警察(London 1829,"bobbies")、义务初等教育。
summary.en: Bismarck introduced social insurance (sickness 1883, accident 1884, old age 1889) to undercut socialism → the start of the European welfare state; Britain’s Liberal reforms brought pensions and national insurance (1906–1911); professional police (London 1829, "bobbies"); compulsory primary schooling.

detail.zh: 国家角色从"守夜人"变成干预社会,这是保守派和自由派都参与的转变。
detail.en: The state shifted from night watchman to active social intervention, a change embraced by conservatives and liberals alike.

summary.zh: 中产阶级改革运动:abolition(英国 1807 禁奴隶贸易、1833 废奴)、temperance(禁酒)、监狱与济贫改革;女权:Women’s Social and Political Union(Emmeline Pankhurst,激进的 suffragettes)。
summary.en: Middle-class reform movements: abolition (Britain banned the slave trade in 1807 and slavery in 1833), temperance, prison and poor-law reform; feminism: the Women’s Social and Political Union (Emmeline Pankhurst’s militant suffragettes).

detail.zh: Florence Nightingale 推动护理职业化;女性进入教师、护士、职员等新职业。New Poor Law(1834)用 workhouses 惩戒贫困。
detail.en: Florence Nightingale professionalized nursing; women entered new jobs as teachers, nurses, and clerks. The New Poor Law (1834) used workhouses to deter poverty.

summary.zh: 中产女权:Barbara Bodichon(已婚女性财产权)、Josephine Butler(反对 Contagious Diseases Acts);社会主义女权:Flora Tristan(工人联合)、Clara Zetkin、Rosa Luxemburg —— 认为女性解放离不开阶级革命。
summary.en: Middle-class feminists: Barbara Bodichon (married women’s property rights) and Josephine Butler (against the Contagious Diseases Acts); socialist feminists: Flora Tristan (workers’ union), Clara Zetkin, and Rosa Luxemburg — who tied women’s liberation to class revolution.

detail.zh: 对比:中产女权争取法律与选举权;社会主义女权强调工人阶级女性的经济处境。还有 Sunday School、互助会(mutual aid societies)、慈善(philanthropy)等社会自救形式。
detail.en: Contrast: middle-class feminists sought legal and voting rights; socialist feminists focused on working-class women’s economic conditions. Sunday Schools, mutual aid societies, and philanthropy were other forms of self-help.

summary.zh: Carlsbad Decrees(1819):审查报刊、监控大学、取缔学生社团(Burschenschaften)→ Concert of Europe 出兵镇压西班牙、Naples 的自由主义起义(Troppau、Verona 会议)。
summary.en: The Carlsbad Decrees (1819): press censorship, university surveillance, banned student fraternities (Burschenschaften) → the Concert of Europe sent troops to crush liberal revolts in Spain and Naples (Congresses of Troppau and Verona).

detail.zh: 英国在 1820 年代逐渐退出干预政策。英国本土:Peterloo Massacre(1819)和 Six Acts 也压制激进派。
detail.en: Britain drifted away from intervention in the 1820s. At home, the Peterloo Massacre (1819) and the Six Acts repressed British radicals.

summary.zh: 希腊独立战争反抗 Ottoman → 英、法、俄出于宗教同情与战略利益支持 → 1830 年独立 = 民族主义在 Concert 体系中的例外胜利;Decembrist Revolt(1825,俄国)被 Nicholas I 镇压。
summary.en: The Greek War of Independence against the Ottomans → Britain, France, and Russia intervened from religious sympathy and strategic interest → independence in 1830 = a nationalist exception the Concert allowed; the Decembrist Revolt (1825) in Russia was crushed by Nicholas I.

detail.zh: Lord Byron 为希腊独立而死,浪漫主义与民族主义结合。
detail.en: Lord Byron died for Greek independence, uniting Romanticism and nationalism.

summary.zh: Charles X 推行反动的 July Ordinances → 巴黎起义 → 资产阶级的"公民国王" Louis-Philippe(July Monarchy);同年比利时脱离荷兰独立;Poland 起义被俄国镇压。
summary.en: Charles X’s reactionary July Ordinances → a Paris uprising → the bourgeois "citizen king" Louis-Philippe (the July Monarchy); the same year Belgium won independence from the Netherlands; a Polish uprising was crushed by Russia.

detail.zh: July Monarchy 选举权仍很窄,只代表富裕资产阶级("Enrich yourselves" —— Guizot)。
detail.en: The July Monarchy’s franchise stayed narrow, serving the wealthy bourgeoisie ("Enrich yourselves" — Guizot).

summary.zh: 原因:歉收与经济萧条("Hungry Forties")+ 自由主义要求宪法与选举权 + 民族主义 → 法国推翻 Louis-Philippe 建 Second Republic → June Days 工人起义被镇压 → 选出 Louis Napoleon 为总统(1852 年称帝 Napoleon III)。
summary.en: Causes: crop failures and depression (the "Hungry Forties") + liberal demands for constitutions and suffrage + nationalism → France overthrew Louis-Philippe for the Second Republic → the June Days workers’ uprising was crushed → Louis Napoleon was elected president (emperor Napoleon III in 1852).

detail.zh: National Workshops 被关闭引发 June Days;中产阶级与工人的联盟破裂是 1848 年失败的关键。
detail.en: Closing the National Workshops triggered the June Days; the split between middle class and workers was key to 1848’s failure.

summary.zh: Vienna 起义 → Metternich 下台、奥地利废除农奴制;Hungary(Kossuth)要求自治 → 俄军帮奥地利镇压;Frankfurt Parliament 想统一德意志,向普鲁士王献"来自贫民窟的王冠"被拒 → 失败。
summary.en: Revolt in Vienna → Metternich fell and Austria abolished serfdom; Hungary under Kossuth demanded autonomy → Russian troops helped Austria crush it; the Frankfurt Parliament tried to unite Germany and offered Frederick William IV a "crown from the gutter," which he refused → failure.

detail.zh: 失败原因:民族之间互相冲突、中产阶级害怕工人激进、军队仍效忠君主。结果:保守派复辟,但农奴制废除、宪法在一些地方保留;此后民族统一转向"现实政治"(Unit 7)。
detail.en: Why it failed: nationalities clashed, the middle class feared radical workers, and armies stayed loyal to monarchs. Results: conservative restoration, but serfdom ended and some constitutions survived; unification turned to Realpolitik (Unit 7).

summary.zh: Burke、Metternich、de Maistre:维护君主、贵族、教会与传统,反对激进变革和民族自决(对多民族帝国是威胁)。
summary.en: Burke, Metternich, de Maistre: defended monarchy, aristocracy, the Church, and tradition; opposed radical change and national self-determination (a threat to multiethnic empires).

detail.zh: 19 世纪后期的保守派学会利用民族主义和福利政策(Bismarck、Disraeli)。
detail.en: Later conservatives learned to harness nationalism and welfare (Bismarck, Disraeli).

summary.zh: 个人自由、宪法、法治、有限选举权(有产者)、laissez-faire;Malthus(人口)与 Ricardo(iron law of wages)为低工资辩护;Bentham 的 utilitarianism:最大多数人的最大幸福;J. S. Mill《On Liberty》并支持女性选举权。
summary.en: Individual liberty, constitutions, rule of law, limited (propertied) suffrage, laissez-faire; Malthus (population) and Ricardo (the iron law of wages) justified low wages; Bentham’s utilitarianism: the greatest good for the greatest number; J. S. Mill’s On Liberty, and support for women’s suffrage.

detail.zh: 自由主义的基础是中产阶级。Mill 和 Harriet Taylor《The Subjection of Women》(1869)。
detail.en: Liberalism’s base was the middle class. Mill and Harriet Taylor’s The Subjection of Women (1869).

summary.zh: Robert Owen(New Lanark 模范工厂社区)、Charles Fourier(phalanxes)、Saint-Simon(技术专家治理)、Louis Blanc(国家工场)—— 用合作与示范社区改造资本主义。
summary.en: Robert Owen (the New Lanark model mill community), Charles Fourier (phalanxes), Saint-Simon (rule by experts), Louis Blanc (national workshops) — reform capitalism through cooperation and model communities.

detail.zh: Marx 称他们为"空想"社会主义,因为不依靠阶级斗争。
detail.en: Marx called them "utopian" because they did not rely on class struggle.

summary.zh: Marx & Engels《Communist Manifesto》(1848):历史是阶级斗争史 → bourgeoisie vs. proletariat → 无产阶级革命 → 无阶级社会;"Workers of the world, unite!"
summary.en: Marx and Engels’s Communist Manifesto (1848): history is the history of class struggle → bourgeoisie vs. proletariat → proletarian revolution → a classless society; "Workers of the world, unite!"

detail.zh: Das Kapital(1867)。First International(1864)。后来分化出 revisionism(Eduard Bernstein:通过议会和改革实现社会主义)和革命派(Lenin)。
detail.en: Das Kapital (1867); the First International (1864). Later split into revisionism (Eduard Bernstein: socialism through elections and reform) and revolutionaries (Lenin).

summary.zh: Anarchism:废除国家本身(Proudhon"财产就是盗窃"、Bakunin);部分无政府主义者采取暗杀;syndicalism:以工会总罢工推翻资本主义(Sorel)。
summary.en: Anarchism: abolish the state itself (Proudhon: "property is theft"; Bakunin); some anarchists turned to assassination; syndicalism: overthrow capitalism through union general strikes (Sorel).

detail.zh: 无政府主义者暗杀了俄国沙皇 Alexander II(1881,People’s Will)、奥地利皇后 Elisabeth 等。
detail.en: Radicals assassinated Tsar Alexander II (1881, People’s Will) and Empress Elisabeth of Austria, among others.

summary.zh: Nationalism:民族应有自己的国家(Mazzini、Herder),前期与自由主义结盟,1848 后被保守派利用;feminism:从要求教育、财产权走向选举权运动。
summary.en: Nationalism: each nation should have its own state (Mazzini, Herder), allied with liberalism early on and co-opted by conservatives after 1848; feminism: from demands for education and property rights to the suffrage movement.

detail.zh: 民族主义的转变是经典 C/C:从自由的、包容的(1848)到保守的、排他的(19 世纪末)。
detail.en: Nationalism’s shift is a classic continuity/change item: from liberal and inclusive (1848) to conservative and exclusive (late 19th century).

summary.zh: 俄国想趁 Ottoman 衰弱南下 → 英、法(及 Piedmont)支持 Ottoman → 俄国战败 → Concert of Europe 瓦解、俄国意识到落后而改革、奥地利因中立被孤立。
summary.en: Russia pushed south against the weakening Ottomans → Britain, France (and Piedmont) backed the Ottomans → Russia lost → the Concert of Europe broke down, Russia saw it must modernize, and Austria, neutral, was isolated.

detail.zh: Florence Nightingale 的战地护理;第一次有战地记者与摄影。Austria 的孤立为意大利和德意志统一创造了机会。
detail.en: Florence Nightingale’s nursing; the first war correspondents and photographs. Austria’s isolation opened the way for Italian and German unification.

summary.zh: 用公民投票称帝,"威权的现代化":Haussmann 重建巴黎、铁路与银行、后期允许工会和议会扩权 → 1870 年普法战争战败被俘 → Third Republic。
summary.en: Became emperor through plebiscites — authoritarian modernization: Haussmann’s Paris, railways and banks, later legal unions and a stronger legislature → captured in the Franco-Prussian War (1870) → the Third Republic.

detail.zh: Paris Commune(1871):巴黎激进派自治,被政府血腥镇压(约 2 万人死亡)。
detail.en: The Paris Commune (1871): radical Parisian self-rule, crushed by the government with some 20,000 killed.

summary.zh: 克里米亚战败暴露落后 → Emancipation of the Serfs(1861)→ 农民获得自由但须付赎金、土地归村社(mir);地方自治会 zemstvos、司法与军事改革 —— 1881 年被激进派暗杀,其子 Alexander III 转向反动。
summary.en: Crimean defeat exposed backwardness → the Emancipation of the Serfs (1861) → peasants were freed but owed redemption payments, with land held by the village commune (mir); local zemstvos, judicial and military reforms — he was assassinated in 1881, and Alexander III turned reactionary.

detail.zh: Russification(强制推广俄语与东正教)和对犹太人的 pogroms 在 Alexander III 时期加剧。
detail.en: Russification (imposing Russian language and Orthodoxy) and pogroms against Jews intensified under Alexander III.

summary.zh: 奥地利被普鲁士击败(1866)后与匈牙利妥协 → Dual Monarchy:两个政府、一个皇帝(Franz Joseph)、共同外交与军事 → 但斯拉夫人等其他民族仍不满。
summary.en: After defeat by Prussia (1866), Austria compromised with Hungary → the Dual Monarchy: two governments, one emperor (Franz Joseph), shared foreign policy and army → yet Slavs and other peoples remained discontented.

detail.zh: Pan-Slavism(俄国支持)在 Balkans 与奥匈冲突,成为一战导火线之一。
detail.en: Pan-Slavism, backed by Russia, clashed with Austria-Hungary in the Balkans — a fuse of World War I.

summary.zh: 犹太军官 Dreyfus 被诬陷叛国 → 法国分裂(Zola《J’Accuse!》)→ 暴露欧洲反犹主义 → Theodor Herzl《The Jewish State》(1896)发起 Zionism:在巴勒斯坦建立犹太国家。
summary.en: Jewish officer Alfred Dreyfus was falsely convicted of treason → France split (Zola’s J’Accuse!) → exposing European antisemitism → Theodor Herzl’s The Jewish State (1896) launched Zionism: a Jewish homeland in Palestine.

detail.zh: Vienna 市长 Karl Lueger 用反犹主义赢得选举,影响了青年 Hitler。反犹主义从宗教偏见转向"种族"偏见。
detail.en: Vienna mayor Karl Lueger won office on antisemitism, influencing the young Hitler. Antisemitism shifted from religious to "racial" prejudice.

summary.zh: 选举权扩大 → 大众政党(社会主义、天主教、民族主义政党)、大众报纸;Ottoman 帝国 Tanzimat 改革与 Young Turks(1908)试图挽救"欧洲病夫",但 Balkans 民族接连独立。
summary.en: Wider suffrage → mass parties (socialist, Catholic, nationalist) and mass newspapers; the Ottoman Tanzimat reforms and the Young Turks (1908) tried to save the "sick man of Europe," but Balkan peoples broke away one after another.

detail.zh: Congress of Berlin(1878)承认 Serbia、Romania、Montenegro 独立;Balkan Wars(1912–1913)。1908 年奥匈吞并 Bosnia-Herzegovina,激怒塞尔维亚。
detail.en: The Congress of Berlin (1878) recognized Serbian, Romanian, and Montenegrin independence; the Balkan Wars followed (1912–1913). Austria-Hungary’s 1908 annexation of Bosnia-Herzegovina enraged Serbia.

summary.zh: Mazzini(Young Italy,浪漫共和理想)失败于 1848 → Cavour(Piedmont 首相,Realpolitik):参加克里米亚战争拉拢法国 → 1859 联法败奥得 Lombardy;Garibaldi 的 Red Shirts 征服南方(两西西里)后交给 Victor Emmanuel II。
summary.en: Mazzini (Young Italy, romantic republicanism) failed in 1848 → Cavour (Piedmont’s prime minister, Realpolitik) joined the Crimean War to win France → with France beat Austria in 1859 to gain Lombardy; Garibaldi’s Red Shirts conquered the south (the Two Sicilies) and handed it to Victor Emmanuel II.

detail.zh: 意大利统一的"心、脑、剑":Mazzini、Cavour、Garibaldi。
detail.en: Italy’s "heart, brain, and sword": Mazzini, Cavour, Garibaldi.

summary.zh: 1861 年意大利王国成立 → 1866 年(普奥战争)得 Venetia → 1870 年(普法战争)法军撤出,得 Rome → 统一完成;但南北差距巨大,教皇拒绝承认。
summary.en: The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861 → Venetia added in 1866 (the Austro-Prussian War) → Rome in 1870 when French troops left (the Franco-Prussian War) → unification complete; but a deep North–South divide remained and the pope refused recognition.

detail.zh: "We have made Italy; now we must make Italians"(d’Azeglio)—— 多数人讲方言,民族认同薄弱。
detail.en: "We have made Italy; now we must make Italians" (d’Azeglio) — most people spoke dialects, and national identity was thin.

summary.zh: Bismarck"blood and iron" → ① 丹麦战争(1864)② Austro-Prussian (Seven Weeks’) War(1866)排除奥地利、建 North German Confederation ③ Franco-Prussian War(1870–1871,Ems Dispatch 挑衅)→ 南德诸邦加入 → 1871 年在 Versailles 镜厅宣布德意志帝国。
summary.en: Bismarck’s "blood and iron" → ① the Danish War (1864) ② the Austro-Prussian (Seven Weeks’) War (1866) expelled Austria and created the North German Confederation ③ the Franco-Prussian War (1870–1871, provoked with the Ems Dispatch) → the southern states joined → the German Empire proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles in 1871.

detail.zh: 德国从法国夺取 Alsace-Lorraine 并索赔 → 法国复仇心理(revanche)。Wilhelm I 为皇帝。
detail.en: Germany took Alsace-Lorraine and an indemnity from France → French revanchism. Wilhelm I became emperor.

summary.zh: 联邦制,Reichstag 男子普选但权力有限,首相只对皇帝负责;Kulturkampf 打压天主教会(后放弃);Anti-Socialist Laws(1878)+ 社会保险 —— 胡萝卜加大棒。
summary.en: A federal empire with a Reichstag elected by universal male suffrage but limited power, and a chancellor answerable only to the emperor; the Kulturkampf against the Catholic Church (later abandoned); Anti-Socialist Laws (1878) + social insurance — carrot and stick.

detail.zh: 变化:有了全国议会和普选;延续:普鲁士容克与军队主导,不是真正的议会民主。
detail.en: Change: a national parliament with universal male suffrage; continuity: Prussian Junkers and the army dominated — not a true parliamentary democracy.

summary.zh: 目标:孤立法国、避免两线作战 → Three Emperors’ League(德奥俄)、Dual Alliance(德奥 1879)、Triple Alliance(+ 意大利 1882)、Reinsurance Treaty(德俄 1887);Congress of Berlin(1878)扮演"诚实的掮客"。
summary.en: Goal: isolate France and avoid a two-front war → the Three Emperors’ League (Germany, Austria, Russia), the Dual Alliance (Germany–Austria, 1879), the Triple Alliance (+ Italy, 1882), the Reinsurance Treaty (Germany–Russia, 1887); the Congress of Berlin (1878) with Bismarck as "honest broker."

detail.zh: Bismarck 认为德国已"饱和",不需要扩张,只要维持现状。
detail.en: Bismarck saw Germany as "satiated," needing only to preserve the status quo.

summary.zh: Wilhelm II 解雇 Bismarck(1890),推行 Weltpolitik、不续签 Reinsurance Treaty、与英国海军竞赛(dreadnoughts)→ Franco-Russian Alliance(1894)、Entente Cordiale(英法 1904)→ Triple Entente(1907)对 Triple Alliance。
summary.en: Wilhelm II dismissed Bismarck (1890), pursued Weltpolitik, let the Reinsurance Treaty lapse, and launched a naval race with Britain (dreadnoughts) → the Franco-Russian Alliance (1894), the Entente Cordiale (1904) → the Triple Entente (1907) vs. the Triple Alliance.

detail.zh: Moroccan Crises(1905、1911)反而巩固了英法协约。这是 Unit 8 一战原因(MAIN)的铺垫。
detail.en: The Moroccan Crises (1905, 1911) only tightened the Anglo-French entente — the setup for WWI’s causes (MAIN) in Unit 8.

summary.zh: Charles Darwin《On the Origin of Species》:natural selection 推动物种进化 → 挑战《创世记》与人类特殊地位,引发宗教与科学冲突;《The Descent of Man》(1871)。
summary.en: Charles Darwin’s On the Origin of Species: natural selection drives evolution → challenged Genesis and humanity’s special place, sparking conflict between science and religion; The Descent of Man (1871).

detail.zh: 天主教会 1864 年的 Syllabus of Errors 谴责现代主义与自由主义;Papal infallibility(1870)。
detail.en: The Catholic Church’s Syllabus of Errors (1864) condemned modernism and liberalism; papal infallibility followed (1870).

summary.zh: Herbert Spencer 把进化论套到社会("survival of the fittest")→ 为自由放任、种族主义、帝国主义辩护,也被用于 eugenics(优生学)和极端民族主义。
summary.en: Herbert Spencer applied evolution to society ("survival of the fittest") → justified laissez-faire, racism, and imperialism, and fed eugenics and extreme nationalism.

detail.zh: 这是对 Darwin 科学的误用,但影响巨大,延续到 20 世纪纳粹种族理论(Unit 8)。
detail.en: A misuse of Darwin’s science, but enormously influential, reaching Nazi racial theory (Unit 8).

summary.zh: Auguste Comte 的 positivism:只有科学方法能获得可靠知识,社会学之父;医学:Pasteur(细菌理论、巴氏消毒)、Koch、Lister(消毒外科);Mendeleev 元素周期表;Faraday、Maxwell(电磁)。
summary.en: Auguste Comte’s positivism: only scientific method yields reliable knowledge; father of sociology; medicine: Pasteur (germ theory, pasteurization), Koch, Lister (antiseptic surgery); Mendeleev’s periodic table; Faraday and Maxwell (electromagnetism).

detail.zh: 这是"进步的时代":寿命延长、城市卫生改善,强化了欧洲人对自身文明优越的信心。
detail.en: The "age of progress": longer lives and cleaner cities strengthened Europeans’ belief in their civilization’s superiority.

summary.zh: 19 世纪浪漫主义继续:绘画 Goya(战争暴行)、Constable、Turner;诗歌 Keats、Shelley;音乐 Wagner(德意志民族神话)、Tchaikovsky、Chopin —— 强调情感、民族、自然。
summary.en: Romanticism carried on into the 19th century: painting — Goya (the horrors of war), Constable, Turner; poetry — Keats, Shelley; music — Wagner (German national myth), Tchaikovsky, Chopin — stressing emotion, nation, and nature.

detail.zh: AMSCO 在 Topic 7.8 把浪漫主义与现实主义放在一起比较;romantic idealism vs. 现实主义的 materialism 与 scientific determinism。
detail.en: AMSCO’s Topic 7.8 compares Romanticism with Realism: romantic idealism vs. Realist materialism and scientific determinism.

summary.zh: Nietzsche:"God is dead",批判基督教道德与理性,呼唤 Übermensch;Freud:潜意识与非理性驱力支配人(《The Interpretation of Dreams》1900);Einstein 相对论(1905)、Planck 量子理论 → Newton 式确定性被动摇。
summary.en: Nietzsche: "God is dead," an attack on Christian morality and reason, a call for the Übermensch; Freud: the unconscious and irrational drives govern people (The Interpretation of Dreams, 1900); Einstein’s relativity (1905) and Planck’s quantum theory → Newtonian certainty shaken.

detail.zh: Marie Curie 的放射性研究;Georges Sorel 强调非理性神话。这些思想为 20 世纪的焦虑与相对主义埋下伏笔。Henri Bergson 强调直觉与"生命冲动",代表世纪末的 irrationalism;Freud 创立 psychoanalysis;Planck 开启 quantum mechanics。
detail.en: Marie Curie’s work on radioactivity; Georges Sorel’s political myths. These ideas foreshadowed 20th-century anxiety and relativism. Henri Bergson stressed intuition and the vital impulse, part of fin-de-siècle irrationalism; Freud founded psychoanalysis; Planck launched quantum mechanics.

summary.zh: 反对浪漫主义的理想化,如实描绘工人与普通人的生活和社会问题:绘画 Gustave Courbet《The Stone Breakers》、Millet;文学 Dickens、Zola、Flaubert、Tolstoy。
summary.en: Rejecting Romantic idealization, it depicted workers’ and ordinary people’s lives and social problems: painting — Gustave Courbet’s The Stone Breakers, Millet; literature — Dickens, Zola, Flaubert, Tolstoy.

detail.zh: Realism 与实证主义、社会问题小说相呼应。摄影的出现也促使画家寻找新方向。其他:讽刺画家 Daumier、Balzac、George Eliot、Dostoevsky;Zola 的 naturalism 更强调遗传与环境决定论。
detail.en: Realism echoed positivism and the social-problem novel. Photography pushed painters to seek new directions. Others: the caricaturist Daumier, Balzac, George Eliot, Dostoevsky; Zola’s naturalism stressed heredity and environment.

summary.zh: Impressionism:捕捉光线与瞬间印象(Monet、Renoir、Degas);Post-Impressionism:强调形式与情感(Van Gogh、Cézanne、Gauguin);20 世纪初 Cubism(Picasso)、Expressionism —— 艺术远离写实。
summary.en: Impressionism: capturing light and fleeting impressions (Monet, Renoir, Degas); Post-Impressionism: emphasizing form and emotion (Van Gogh, Cézanne, Gauguin); early 20th-century Cubism (Picasso) and Expressionism — art moved away from realism.

detail.zh: Gauguin 去 Tahiti、Picasso 受非洲面具影响 —— 帝国主义也影响了欧洲艺术(Japonisme)。Matisse 的 Fauvism 用强烈色彩。
detail.en: Gauguin went to Tahiti and Picasso drew on African masks — imperialism shaped European art too (Japonisme). Matisse’s Fauvism used bold, nonnaturalistic color.

summary.zh: 经济:原料(橡胶、棉花、矿产)、市场与投资(Hobson、Lenin 的经济解释);政治:民族威望、海军基地、大国竞争;文化:传教、"civilizing mission"、"White Man’s Burden"(Kipling);Social Darwinism 种族主义。
summary.en: Economic: raw materials (rubber, cotton, minerals), markets, and investment (Hobson’s and Lenin’s economic explanations); political: national prestige, naval bases, great-power rivalry; cultural: missionaries, the "civilizing mission," the "White Man’s Burden" (Kipling); Social Darwinist racism.

detail.zh: Lenin《Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism》(1916)把帝国主义解释为资本主义寻找投资出路。法国称之为 mission civilisatrice;民族自大(chauvinism、national aggrandizement)也是动机。
detail.en: Lenin’s Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism (1916) explained empire as capitalism’s search for investment outlets. The French called it the mission civilisatrice; chauvinism and national aggrandizement were motives too.

summary.zh: Steamships 和铁路深入内陆;quinine 防疟疾让欧洲人能进入热带非洲;Maxim gun(机枪)带来压倒性军事优势;电报与 Suez Canal(1869)缩短距离。
summary.en: Steamships and railways penetrated interiors; quinine against malaria let Europeans survive in tropical Africa; the Maxim gun gave overwhelming firepower; the telegraph and the Suez Canal (1869) shrank distances.

detail.zh: Battle of Omdurman(1898):英军用机枪杀死约 1 万苏丹人,自损不到 50 人。还有后膛枪(breech-loading rifle)、Minié ball 子弹和麻醉(anesthesia)等医学进步。
detail.en: At Omdurman (1898) British machine guns killed some 10,000 Sudanese for fewer than 50 British losses. Also breech-loading rifles, the Minié ball, and medical advances such as anesthesia.

summary.zh: Bismarck 召开 Berlin Conference:规定"effective occupation"才能声索领土,无一位非洲人参加 → Scramble for Africa:到 1914 年只有 Ethiopia 和 Liberia 保持独立。
summary.en: Bismarck hosted the Berlin Conference: claims required "effective occupation," with no Africans present → the Scramble for Africa: by 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent.

detail.zh: Ethiopia 在 Adwa(1896)击败意大利。人为边界无视民族分布,影响至今。
detail.en: Ethiopia defeated Italy at Adwa (1896). Artificial borders ignored ethnic patterns, with effects lasting to today.

summary.zh: 比利时国王 Leopold II 把 Congo 当私人领地,强迫劳动采橡胶,用砍手等暴行 → 估计死亡数百万 → 国际舆论谴责(E. D. Morel、Conrad《Heart of Darkness》)→ 1908 年移交比利时政府。
summary.en: Belgium’s Leopold II ran the Congo as his personal property, forcing people to harvest rubber under atrocities such as severed hands → millions died → international outcry (E. D. Morel; Conrad’s Heart of Darkness) → transferred to the Belgian state in 1908.

detail.zh: Congo 是帝国主义残暴的极端例证,也是早期国际人权运动的案例。Morel 创立 Congo Reform Association。
detail.en: The Congo is the extreme example of imperial brutality and an early human-rights campaign. Morel founded the Congo Reform Association.

summary.zh: Sepoy Mutiny(1857)后东印度公司被取代,英国王室直接统治印度(British Raj,1858);1885 年 Indian National Congress 成立;南非 Boer War(1899–1902)英国艰难获胜、用集中营。
summary.en: After the Sepoy Mutiny (1857) the East India Company was replaced by direct crown rule (the British Raj, 1858); the Indian National Congress formed in 1885; Britain won the Boer War in South Africa (1899–1902) only with difficulty, using concentration camps.

detail.zh: 印度是"皇冠上的明珠",原棉出口、英国制成品进口,本土纺织业受损。Boer War 暴露英国军力问题,促使其结束"光荣孤立"。非洲抵抗:Anglo-Zulu War(1879)中 Zulu 在 Isandlwana 重创英军。
detail.en: India was the "jewel in the crown," exporting raw cotton and importing British goods, hurting local textiles. The Boer War exposed British weakness and helped end "splendid isolation." African resistance: in the Anglo-Zulu War (1879) the Zulu crushed a British force at Isandlwana.

summary.zh: Opium Wars(1839–1842、1856–1860)→ 不平等条约、通商口岸、spheres of influence;Boxer Rebellion(1900)被八国联军镇压;对比:Japan 的 Meiji Restoration(1868)主动西化,成为帝国主义国家,1905 年击败俄国。
summary.en: The Opium Wars (1839–1842, 1856–1860) → unequal treaties, treaty ports, and spheres of influence; the Boxer Rebellion (1900) was crushed by eight powers; contrast Japan’s Meiji Restoration (1868), which Westernized deliberately, became imperial itself, and beat Russia in 1905.

detail.zh: 美国提出 Open Door Policy。日俄战争是第一次亚洲国家在现代战争中击败欧洲大国,鼓舞了反殖民运动。
detail.en: The U.S. proposed the Open Door Policy. The Russo-Japanese War was the first modern defeat of a European power by an Asian one, inspiring anticolonial movements.

summary.zh: 殖民争夺加剧大国紧张:Fashoda Crisis(英法 1898)、Moroccan Crises(德法 1905、1911);批评者:J. A. Hobson《Imperialism》(1902)、Lenin、反帝国主义社会主义者。
summary.en: Colonial competition heightened tension: the Fashoda Crisis (Britain–France, 1898) and the Moroccan Crises (Germany–France, 1905, 1911); critics: J. A. Hobson’s Imperialism (1902), Lenin, and anti-imperialist socialists.

detail.zh: Fashoda 以法国让步结束,英法反而走向 Entente;Morocco 危机让英法更紧密地对抗德国。
detail.en: Fashoda ended with France backing down and Britain and France moving toward the Entente; the Moroccan Crises bound them more tightly against Germany.

summary.zh: Militarism(军备竞赛、英德海军竞赛、Schlieffen Plan)+ Alliances(Triple Entente vs. Triple Alliance)+ Imperialism(摩洛哥危机)+ Nationalism(Pan-Slavism、Balkans"火药桶")。
summary.en: Militarism (arms race, the Anglo-German naval race, the Schlieffen Plan) + alliances (the Triple Entente vs. the Triple Alliance) + imperialism (the Moroccan Crises) + nationalism (Pan-Slavism, the Balkan "powder keg").

detail.zh: Balkan Wars(1912–1913)让 Serbia 强大,奥匈视之为威胁。
detail.en: The Balkan Wars (1912–1913) strengthened Serbia, which Austria-Hungary saw as a threat.

summary.zh: 塞尔维亚民族主义者 Gavrilo Princip 刺杀奥匈皇储 Franz Ferdinand → 德国给奥匈"blank check" → 奥匈对塞宣战 → 俄国动员 → 德国执行 Schlieffen Plan 经比利时攻法 → 英国参战。
summary.en: Serbian nationalist Gavrilo Princip assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand → Germany gave Austria-Hungary a "blank check" → Austria declared war on Serbia → Russia mobilized → Germany launched the Schlieffen Plan through Belgium against France → Britain entered.

detail.zh: 联盟体系把局部冲突变成全面战争。各国民众起初热情支持("over by Christmas")。
detail.en: The alliance system turned a local crisis into a general war. Crowds at first cheered ("over by Christmas").

summary.zh: Battle of the Marne(1914)挡住德军 → 西线陷入堑壕战僵局 → Verdun、Somme(1916)数十万伤亡;新技术:机枪、毒气、坦克、飞机、潜艇。
summary.en: The Battle of the Marne (1914) halted Germany → stalemate in the trenches of the Western Front → Verdun and the Somme (1916) with hundreds of thousands of casualties; new technology: machine guns, poison gas, tanks, aircraft, submarines.

detail.zh: 东线更具机动性:Tannenberg(1914)德国大胜俄国。Gallipoli(1915)协约国失败。
detail.en: The Eastern Front was more mobile: Germany crushed Russia at Tannenberg (1914). The Allies failed at Gallipoli (1915).

title.zh: Total war on the home front
title.en: Total war on the home front

summary.zh: 政府控制经济(配给、生产计划)、宣传与审查、全面征兵;女性进入工厂和服务业 → 战后多国给予女性选举权(英 1918、德 1919)。
summary.en: Governments directed economies (rationing, production planning), used propaganda and censorship, and conscripted mass armies; women entered factories and services → many countries granted women suffrage after the war (Britain 1918, Germany 1919).

detail.zh: 变化:国家权力空前扩张;延续:战后许多女性被要求回到家庭。
detail.en: Change: unprecedented state power; continuity: many women were pushed back into the home after the war.

summary.zh: 殖民地士兵与劳工参战(印度、非洲);Ottoman 参战,中东战场(Lawrence of Arabia、Armenian Genocide 1915);德国无限制潜艇战 + Zimmermann Telegram → 美国 1917 年参战;俄国退出 → 1918 年德国春季攻势失败 → 11 月 11 日停战。
summary.en: Colonial soldiers and laborers fought (India, Africa); the Ottomans joined, opening a Middle East front (Lawrence of Arabia; the Armenian Genocide, 1915); German unrestricted submarine warfare + the Zimmermann Telegram → the U.S. entered in 1917; Russia left → Germany’s 1918 spring offensive failed → armistice on November 11.

detail.zh: 1918 年流感大流行又夺去数千万人生命。
detail.en: The 1918 influenza pandemic then killed tens of millions more.

summary.zh: 日俄战争失败 + Bloody Sunday(军队向请愿工人开枪)→ 罢工起义 → Nicholas II 发布 October Manifesto,设立 Duma → 但很快架空杜马。
summary.en: Defeat by Japan + Bloody Sunday (troops fired on petitioning workers) → strikes and revolt → Nicholas II’s October Manifesto created the Duma → which he soon sidelined.

detail.zh: Stolypin 的土地改革试图培养富农(kulaks)以稳定农村。
detail.en: Stolypin’s land reforms tried to create prosperous peasants (kulaks) to stabilize the countryside.

summary.zh: 一战惨败、粮食短缺、Rasputin 丑闻 → Petrograd 罢工与兵变 → Nicholas II 退位 → Provisional Government(Kerensky)与 Petrograd Soviet "双重政权";临时政府继续作战失去民心。
summary.en: Military disaster, food shortages, and the Rasputin scandal → strikes and mutiny in Petrograd → Nicholas II abdicated → "dual power" between the Provisional Government (Kerensky) and the Petrograd Soviet; the Provisional Government’s decision to keep fighting cost it support.

detail.zh: 德国用密封火车把 Lenin 送回俄国,希望他让俄国退出战争。
detail.en: Germany shipped Lenin home in a sealed train, hoping he would take Russia out of the war.

summary.zh: Lenin 的 April Theses:"Peace, Land, and Bread"、"All power to the soviets" → Bolsheviks(Trotsky 组织红卫兵)夺取冬宫 → 解散立宪会议 → Treaty of Brest-Litovsk(1918)割地退出一战。
summary.en: Lenin’s April Theses: "Peace, Land, and Bread" and "All power to the soviets" → the Bolsheviks, organized by Trotsky, seized the Winter Palace → dissolved the Constituent Assembly → the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (1918) gave up vast territory to leave the war.

detail.zh: Lenin 的 vanguard party 理论:职业革命者带领工人,修正了 Marx 对"成熟资本主义国家先革命"的预测。
detail.en: Lenin’s vanguard party — professional revolutionaries leading the workers — revised Marx’s expectation that revolution would start in advanced capitalist states.

summary.zh: Reds vs. Whites 内战(外国干涉)→ War Communism:征粮、国有化、Cheka 恐怖 → 红军胜 → 经济崩溃与 Kronstadt 兵变 → NEP(1921):允许小规模私营与农民出售余粮 —— "一步后退"。
summary.en: Reds vs. Whites civil war (with foreign intervention) → War Communism: grain requisitioning, nationalization, Cheka terror → the Reds won → economic collapse and the Kronstadt mutiny → the NEP (1921) allowed small private trade and peasant sales — a "step back."

detail.zh: 1922 年成立 USSR;Romanov 一家被处决(1918)。Lenin 1924 年去世后 Stalin 击败 Trotsky。
detail.en: The USSR was founded in 1922; the Romanovs were executed (1918). After Lenin died in 1924, Stalin outmaneuvered Trotsky.

title.zh: Wilson’s Fourteen Points vs. the Big Three
title.en: Wilson’s Fourteen Points vs. the Big Three

summary.zh: Wilson 的 Fourteen Points:self-determination、公开外交、裁军、League of Nations;Clemenceau(法)要惩罚德国、保障安全;Lloyd George(英)介于两者;Orlando(意)要领土。
summary.en: Wilson’s Fourteen Points: self-determination, open diplomacy, disarmament, a League of Nations; Clemenceau (France) wanted to punish Germany and secure France; Lloyd George (Britain) stood between; Orlando (Italy) wanted territory.

detail.zh: 德国和苏俄都没有被邀请参加谈判。
detail.en: Neither Germany nor Soviet Russia was invited to negotiate.

summary.zh: War Guilt Clause (Article 231)、巨额赔款、军队限 10 万人、莱茵兰非军事化、Alsace-Lorraine 还法、失去殖民地 → 德国视之为"Diktat",为 Hitler 提供宣传武器。
summary.en: The War Guilt Clause (Article 231), huge reparations, an army capped at 100,000, a demilitarized Rhineland, Alsace-Lorraine to France, loss of colonies → Germans saw a "Diktat," a gift to Hitler’s propaganda.

detail.zh: Keynes《The Economic Consequences of the Peace》批评赔款不切实际。美国参议院拒绝批准条约,未加入 League。
detail.en: Keynes’s The Economic Consequences of the Peace called reparations unrealistic. The U.S. Senate rejected the treaty and the League.

summary.zh: 四大帝国瓦解 → 新国家:Poland、Czechoslovakia、Yugoslavia、Baltic 国家、Austria、Hungary(但少数民族问题未解决);Ottoman 领土成为英法 mandates(Syria、Iraq、Palestine)→ 殖民地对自决的失望。
summary.en: Four empires collapsed → new states: Poland, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia, the Baltic states, Austria, Hungary (with unresolved minorities); Ottoman lands became British and French mandates (Syria, Iraq, Palestine) → colonial peoples’ disappointment over self-determination.

detail.zh: Balfour Declaration(1917)支持在巴勒斯坦建立犹太民族家园,与对阿拉伯人的承诺矛盾。Atatürk 建立土耳其共和国(1923)。
detail.en: The Balfour Declaration (1917) backed a Jewish national home in Palestine, clashing with promises to Arabs. Atatürk founded the Turkish Republic (1923).
