summary.zh: Weimar 背负"背后捅刀"神话 → 1923 年 Ruhr 被占与恶性通胀 → Dawes Plan 美国贷款带来短暂稳定 → 1929 年华尔街股灾、美国资金撤回 → 大规模失业 → 极端政党(纳粹、共产党)得票激增。
summary.en: Weimar carried the "stab in the back" myth → the 1923 Ruhr occupation and hyperinflation → the Dawes Plan’s U.S. loans brought brief stability → the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the withdrawal of U.S. capital → mass unemployment → surging votes for extremists (Nazis, Communists).

detail.zh: 大萧条应对:英国、法国用紧缩与关税;Keynes《General Theory》(1936)主张政府赤字支出;Sweden 的社会民主福利;法国 Popular Front(Léon Blum,1936)。各国放弃金本位(gold standard)、货币贬值;投机(speculation)是股灾原因之一。
detail.en: Responses: Britain and France used austerity and tariffs; Keynes’s General Theory (1936) urged deficit spending; Sweden’s social-democratic welfare; France’s Popular Front (Léon Blum, 1936). Countries abandoned the gold standard and depreciated their currencies; speculation helped cause the crash.

summary.zh: 战后失望("残缺的胜利")+ 怕共产主义 → Mussolini 的 Blackshirts March on Rome(1922)→ 一党独裁、corporatism(国家协调劳资)、Lateran Accords(1929)与教皇和解;1935 年入侵 Ethiopia。
summary.en: Postwar disappointment (the "mutilated victory") + fear of communism → Mussolini’s Blackshirts made the March on Rome (1922) → one-party dictatorship, corporatism (state-managed labor and capital), the Lateran Accords (1929) with the pope; invaded Ethiopia in 1935.

detail.zh: 法西斯主义:极端民族主义、反共、反自由主义、崇尚暴力与国家。League 对入侵 Ethiopia 的制裁软弱。
detail.en: Fascism: extreme nationalism, anticommunism, antiliberalism, glorification of violence and the state. The League’s sanctions over Ethiopia were weak.

summary.zh: 纳粹成为最大党 → Hitler 合法出任总理(1933)→ Reichstag 大火 → Enabling Act 获独裁权 → 一党国家、Gestapo、SS;Nuremberg Laws(1935)剥夺犹太人公民权 → Kristallnacht(1938);重整军备与公共工程消除失业。
summary.en: The Nazis became the largest party → Hitler was legally appointed chancellor (1933) → the Reichstag fire → the Enabling Act gave him dictatorial power → one-party state, the Gestapo, the SS; the Nuremberg Laws (1935) stripped Jews of citizenship → Kristallnacht (1938); rearmament and public works ended unemployment.

detail.zh: Mein Kampf:种族、Lebensraum、反犹。Night of the Long Knives(1934)清洗 SA。女性被定位于"Kinder, Küche, Kirche"。宣传部长 Joseph Goebbels 打造领袖崇拜(cult of personality)。
detail.en: Mein Kampf: race, Lebensraum, antisemitism. The Night of the Long Knives (1934) purged the SA. Women were assigned "Kinder, Küche, Kirche." Propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels built a cult of personality around Hitler.

summary.zh: Five-Year Plans:强制快速工业化(重工业)→ collectivization 农业、消灭 kulaks → 饥荒(乌克兰 Holodomor,数百万人死亡)→ Great Purge(1936–1938)、作秀审判、Gulag 劳改营。
summary.en: Five-Year Plans forced rapid industrialization (heavy industry) → collectivization of agriculture and "liquidation" of the kulaks → famine (Ukraine’s Holodomor, millions dead) → the Great Purge (1936–1938), show trials, and Gulag labor camps.

detail.zh: 结果:苏联成为工业大国(为二战提供基础),代价是巨大的人命损失。Socialist Realism 管控艺术。
detail.en: Result: the USSR became an industrial power (a base for WWII) at an enormous human cost. Socialist Realism controlled the arts.

summary.en: The Republic (Popular Front) vs. Franco’s Nationalists → Germany and Italy aided Franco (the bombing of Guernica, painted by Picasso), the USSR aided the Republic, Britain and France stayed out → Franco won; a rehearsal for WWII.

detail.zh: 国际纵队(International Brigades)志愿者参战(Orwell《Homage to Catalonia》)。
detail.en: International Brigades of volunteers fought for the Republic (Orwell’s Homage to Catalonia).

summary.zh: "Lost Generation"与战后幻灭(Remarque《All Quiet on the Western Front》);艺术:Dada、Surrealism(Dalí)、Bauhaus;大众文化:电影、广播成为宣传工具(Riefenstahl《Triumph of the Will》)。
summary.en: The "Lost Generation" and postwar disillusionment (Remarque’s All Quiet on the Western Front); art: Dada, Surrealism (Dalí), the Bauhaus; mass culture: film and radio became propaganda tools (Riefenstahl’s Triumph of the Will).

detail.zh: Freud、Einstein 的思想普及,传统确定性崩溃。Weimar Berlin 文化繁荣与纳粹的"堕落艺术"清洗形成对比。
detail.en: Freud’s and Einstein’s ideas spread as old certainties collapsed. Weimar Berlin’s cultural flowering contrasts with the Nazi purge of "degenerate art."

summary.zh: Einstein 相对论 + Bohr、Heisenberg(uncertainty principle)、Schrödinger 的量子力学 → 宇宙不再是 Newton 式确定的机器;Fermi 等人的核物理 → 原子弹(Manhattan Project,1945)。
summary.en: Einstein’s relativity + quantum mechanics from Bohr, Heisenberg (the uncertainty principle), and Schrödinger → the universe was no longer a Newtonian machine of certainties; nuclear physics by Fermi and others → the atomic bomb (the Manhattan Project, 1945).

detail.zh: 科学的不确定性与战后对科技的恐惧(核武)相呼应。许多犹太科学家逃离纳粹德国。
detail.en: Scientific uncertainty echoed postwar fear of technology (nuclear weapons). Many Jewish scientists fled Nazi Germany.

summary.zh: 重整军备(1935)→ 进驻莱茵兰(1936)→ Anschluss 吞并奥地利(1938)→ Munich Agreement(1938):Chamberlain 同意割让 Sudetenland("peace for our time")→ 1939 年 3 月吞并整个捷克 → 绥靖破产。
summary.en: Rearmament (1935) → remilitarized the Rhineland (1936) → Anschluss with Austria (1938) → the Munich Agreement (1938): Chamberlain conceded the Sudetenland ("peace for our time") → Hitler took the rest of Czechoslovakia in March 1939 → appeasement collapsed.

detail.zh: 为什么绥靖:一战创伤与和平主义、英法军备不足、认为 Versailles 对德国过苛、更怕共产主义。
detail.en: Why appease: WWI trauma and pacifism, unready militaries, a sense Versailles had been too harsh, greater fear of communism.

summary.zh: Nazi-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact(1939 年 8 月,含秘密瓜分东欧条款)→ 9 月 1 日德国闪击 Poland(blitzkrieg)→ 英法宣战 → 苏联从东面入侵 Poland。
summary.en: The Nazi-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact (August 1939, with secret terms dividing Eastern Europe) → Germany’s blitzkrieg invasion of Poland on September 1 → Britain and France declared war → the USSR invaded Poland from the east.

detail.zh: 条约让 Hitler 避免两线作战;苏联还吞并了 Baltic 国家。
detail.en: The pact spared Hitler a two-front war; the USSR also annexed the Baltic states.

title.zh: Fall of France, Battle of Britain, Barbarossa
title.en: Fall of France, Battle of Britain, Barbarossa

summary.zh: 1940 年法国沦陷(Vichy 傀儡政权)→ Battle of Britain:RAF 挫败德国空袭,Churchill 坚持抵抗 → 1941 年 6 月 Operation Barbarossa 入侵苏联 → 12 月珍珠港,美国参战。
summary.en: The fall of France in 1940 (the collaborationist Vichy regime) → the Battle of Britain: the RAF defeated the Luftwaffe as Churchill fought on → Operation Barbarossa, the invasion of the USSR, in June 1941 → Pearl Harbor in December brought the U.S. in.

detail.zh: Lend-Lease 美国援助英苏。东线是二战最血腥的战场,苏联死亡约 2700 万人。Axis powers:德、意、日;同盟国领袖 Churchill、FDR、Stalin。
detail.en: Lend-Lease supplied Britain and the USSR. The Eastern Front was the bloodiest theater; Soviet deaths reached about 27 million. The Axis powers: Germany, Italy, Japan; Allied leaders Churchill, FDR, and Stalin.

summary.zh: 盟军重要转折与胜利包括：El Alamein（1942）；Stalingrad（1942–1943，德军在东线的重大失败与转折）；登陆意大利（1943）；D-Day（1944 年 6 月 6 日，在法国开辟新的西线战场）；苏军攻克 Berlin；V-E Day（1945 年 5 月 8 日）。
summary.en: Key Allied turning points and victories included El Alamein (1942); Stalingrad (1942–1943), a pivotal German defeat and turning point on the Eastern Front; the invasion of Italy (1943); D-Day (June 6, 1944), opening a new front in France; Soviet capture of Berlin; and V-E Day (May 8, 1945).

detail.zh: 战时会议:Tehran(1943)、Yalta(1945 年 2 月,东欧"自由选举"承诺)、Potsdam(1945 年 7 月)→ 分歧埋下冷战种子(Unit 9)。
detail.en: Wartime conferences: Tehran (1943), Yalta (February 1945, promises of "free elections" in Eastern Europe), Potsdam (July 1945) → disagreements that seeded the Cold War (Unit 9).

summary.zh: 逐步升级:Nuremberg Laws(1935)→ Kristallnacht(1938)→ 犹太人隔离区 ghettos → 入侵苏联后 Einsatzgruppen 机动屠杀 → Wannsee Conference(1942)规划"Final Solution" → Auschwitz 等灭绝营 → 约 600 万犹太人被杀。
summary.en: Step-by-step escalation: the Nuremberg Laws (1935) → Kristallnacht (1938) → ghettos → after the invasion of the USSR, Einsatzgruppen mobile killing squads → the Wannsee Conference (1942) organized the "Final Solution" → death camps such as Auschwitz → about six million Jews murdered.

detail.zh: 受害者还有 Roma、残疾人、同性恋者、斯拉夫人、政治犯。战后 Nuremberg Trials 审判纳粹领导人,确立"反人类罪"。
detail.en: Other victims: Roma, disabled people, gay men, Slavs, political prisoners. The postwar Nuremberg Trials prosecuted Nazi leaders and established "crimes against humanity."

summary.zh: 德国战败后，德国与 Berlin 于 1945 年分为四个占领区。苏联在东欧支持建立共产党政权；Churchill 于 1946 年发表“Iron Curtain”演讲。1949 年德国分裂为 FRG（西德）与 GDR（东德）。
summary.en: After Germany’s defeat, Germany and Berlin were divided into four occupation zones in 1945. The Soviet Union supported communist regimes in Eastern Europe; Churchill gave his Iron Curtain speech in 1946. Germany split into the FRG (West Germany) and GDR (East Germany) in 1949.

detail.zh: Yalta 承诺东欧自由选举,但苏军占领下没有兑现。
detail.en: Yalta promised free elections in Eastern Europe, but under Soviet occupation they never happened.

title.zh: Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, Berlin Airlift
title.en: Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, Berlin Airlift

summary.zh: Truman Doctrine(1947):containment,援助希腊、土耳其抵抗共产主义;Marshall Plan:约 130 亿美元重建西欧(苏联拒绝,另建 COMECON);Berlin Blockade → Berlin Airlift(1948–1949)。
summary.en: The Truman Doctrine (1947): containment, aiding Greece and Turkey against communism; the Marshall Plan: about $13 billion to rebuild Western Europe (the USSR refused and created COMECON); the Berlin Blockade → the Berlin Airlift (1948–1949).

detail.zh: Marshall Plan 促进了西欧经济奇迹和合作,也让西欧与美国紧密绑定。
detail.en: The Marshall Plan fueled Western Europe’s economic miracle and cooperation and bound it tightly to the U.S.

summary.en: NATO (1949): collective defense for the U.S., Canada, and Western Europe; the Warsaw Pact (1955): the USSR and Eastern Europe; a nuclear arms race, with the Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) as the most dangerous moment.

detail.zh: 西德 1955 年加入 NATO,是 Warsaw Pact 成立的直接原因。
detail.en: West Germany’s entry into NATO in 1955 directly prompted the Warsaw Pact.

summary.zh: Khrushchev 的"秘密报告"谴责斯大林(de-Stalinization)→ 东欧燃起希望 → Hungarian Revolution(Imre Nagy 宣布退出华约)→ 苏军坦克镇压,西方没有干预。
summary.en: Khrushchev’s "Secret Speech" denounced Stalin (de-Stalinization) → hope spread in Eastern Europe → the Hungarian Revolution (Imre Nagy announced withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact) → crushed by Soviet tanks while the West did not intervene.

detail.zh: 同年 Poland 的骚动以有限让步(Gomułka)收场。变化:恐怖减弱;延续:苏联不容许脱离集团。
detail.en: That year Polish unrest ended with limited concessions (Gomułka). Change: less terror; continuity: no exit from the bloc allowed.

summary.en: Huge numbers of East Germans, especially skilled workers, fled west through Berlin → East Germany built the Berlin Wall (1961) → the symbol of the Cold War; Kennedy’s "Ich bin ein Berliner" (1963).

detail.zh: 西德的 Ostpolitik(Willy Brandt,1970 年代)缓和与东方的关系。
detail.en: West Germany’s Ostpolitik (Willy Brandt, 1970s) eased relations with the East.

summary.zh: Alexander Dubček"socialism with a human face"(放松审查、经济改革)→ 华约军队入侵捷克 → Brezhnev Doctrine:苏联有权干预任何偏离社会主义的国家。
summary.en: Alexander Dubček’s "socialism with a human face" (eased censorship, economic reform) → Warsaw Pact forces invaded Czechoslovakia → the Brezhnev Doctrine: the USSR could intervene wherever socialism was threatened.

detail.zh: 1970 年代 détente 与 Helsinki Accords(1975):承认战后边界,同时承诺人权 —— 东欧异见者借此施压。
detail.en: The 1970s brought détente and the Helsinki Accords (1975): recognition of postwar borders in exchange for human-rights pledges that Eastern dissidents later used.

summary.zh: 英国 Labour 政府(Attlee)建立 National Health Service(1948)、国有化重要产业;西德 Adenauer 的 Christian Democrats 与"social market economy"(Wirtschaftswunder)—— 战后共识:混合经济 + 社会保障。
summary.en: Britain’s Labour government (Attlee) created the National Health Service (1948) and nationalized key industries; West Germany’s Adenauer and the Christian Democrats built a "social market economy" (the Wirtschaftswunder) — the postwar consensus: mixed economy + social security.

detail.zh: France:de Gaulle 的 Fifth Republic(1958)强总统制、独立外交、退出 NATO 军事指挥(1966)。"从摇篮到坟墓"(cradle-to-grave)的社会保障。
detail.en: France: de Gaulle’s Fifth Republic (1958) with a strong presidency and independent foreign policy, leaving NATO’s military command (1966). "Cradle-to-grave" social security.

summary.zh: 婴儿潮一代大学生不满大学体制、消费社会、越战与保守道德 → Paris May 1968 学生运动与大罢工几乎推翻 de Gaulle;各地反战、反文化运动。
summary.en: Baby-boom students rejected rigid universities, consumer society, the Vietnam War, and conservative morality → the Paris May 1968 student revolt and general strike nearly toppled de Gaulle; antiwar and counterculture movements spread.

detail.zh: 政治上很快平息,但长期改变了社会风气(性别、个人自由、环保、新左派)。
detail.en: Politically it subsided quickly, but it lastingly changed social attitudes (gender, personal freedom, environmentalism, the New Left).

summary.zh: 1973 年 OPEC 石油禁运 → stagflation(滞胀)→ 战后共识动摇 → Margaret Thatcher(1979–1990)推行 neoliberalism:私有化、削弱工会(1984 煤矿罢工)、减税、削减福利。
summary.en: The 1973 OPEC oil embargo → stagflation → the postwar consensus faltered → Margaret Thatcher (1979–1990) pursued neoliberalism: privatization, curbing unions (the 1984 miners’ strike), tax cuts, welfare restraint.

detail.zh: 变化:市场化与私有化;延续:NHS 等核心福利制度保留。Green parties 在 1980 年代兴起(西德 Die Grünen)。
detail.en: Change: markets and privatization; continuity: core welfare such as the NHS survived. Green parties rose in the 1980s (West Germany’s Die Grünen).

summary.zh: Schuman Plan → European Coal and Steel Community(1951,法德煤钢共管防止再战)→ Treaty of Rome(1957)建立 EEC 共同市场 → Maastricht Treaty(1992/1993)建立 European Union → 欧元(1999/2002)。
summary.en: The Schuman Plan → the European Coal and Steel Community (1951, pooling French and German coal and steel to prevent war) → the Treaty of Rome (1957) created the EEC common market → the Maastricht Treaty (1992/1993) created the European Union → the euro (1999/2002).

detail.zh: Jean Monnet 是"欧洲之父"。英国 1973 年加入,2016 年公投 Brexit、2020 年退出。2004 年东扩吸纳前共产主义国家。
detail.en: Jean Monnet was the "father of Europe." Britain joined in 1973, voted for Brexit in 2016, and left in 2020. The 2004 enlargement took in former communist states.

summary.zh: Simone de Beauvoir《The Second Sex》(1949):"女人不是天生的,而是后天形成的" → 1960–70 年代要求同工同酬、生育权(避孕药、堕胎合法化)、离婚自由、反对家庭暴力。
summary.en: Simone de Beauvoir’s The Second Sex (1949): "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman" → in the 1960s–70s demands for equal pay, reproductive rights (the pill, legal abortion), easier divorce, and protection from domestic violence.

detail.zh: First wave 争取选举权;second wave 争取社会与经济平等。女性政治领袖:Thatcher、Angela Merkel。东欧女性高就业率但承担"双重负担"。女性领导人还有 Ireland 的 Mary Robinson、法国 Édith Cresson;避孕药(birth control pill)与 IVF 改变生育。
detail.en: The first wave sought the vote; the second wave social and economic equality. Women leaders: Thatcher, Angela Merkel. Eastern-bloc women worked in high numbers but carried a "double burden." Other women leaders: Ireland’s Mary Robinson and France’s Édith Cresson; the birth control pill and IVF transformed reproduction.

summary.zh: Lech Wałęsa 领导 Gdańsk 船厂工人于 1980 年成立独立工会 Solidarity；1981 年戒严未将其摧毁，教皇 John Paul II 等提供支持。1989 年举行参议院完全自由、众议院部分自由的选举，Solidarity 在可竞争席位中大胜。
summary.en: Lech Wałęsa and Gdańsk shipyard workers founded the independent Solidarity union in 1980; martial law in 1981 failed to destroy it, and Pope John Paul II supported the movement. In 1989, fully free Senate and partly free Sejm elections brought Solidarity sweeping victories in the contested seats.

detail.en: Poland got the first non-communist government in the bloc, setting off a chain reaction.

summary.en: Gorbachev: glasnost (openness, free speech) + perestroika (economic restructuring) → abandoned the Brezhnev Doctrine (the "Sinatra Doctrine") → Eastern Europe could choose its own way → reform exposed failures and unleashed nationalism.

detail.zh: 背景:经济停滞、阿富汗战争(1979–1989)消耗、与 Reagan 的军备竞赛、Chernobyl(1986)。
detail.en: Background: economic stagnation, the drain of the Afghan war (1979–1989), the arms race with Reagan, and Chernobyl (1986).

summary.en: Peaceful transitions in Poland and Hungary → the fall of the Berlin Wall on November 9 → Czechoslovakia’s Velvet Revolution (Václav Havel) → Romania violently overthrew Ceaușescu → German reunification in 1990.

detail.zh: 除 Romania 外几乎都是和平革命。捷克斯洛伐克 1993 年和平分为两国(Velvet Divorce)。
detail.en: Apart from Romania, the revolutions were largely peaceful. Czechoslovakia split peacefully in 1993 (the Velvet Divorce).

detail.en: Putin (from 2000) recentralized power; the Chechen wars; Crimea annexed in 2014 and full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

summary.zh: Tito 死后民族矛盾上升 → Slobodan Milošević 的塞尔维亚民族主义 → 斯洛文尼亚、克罗地亚、Bosnia 独立 → Bosnia 战争中的 ethnic cleansing,Srebrenica 屠杀(1995,约 8000 名穆斯林男性)→ Dayton Accords;1999 年 NATO 为 Kosovo 轰炸塞尔维亚。
summary.en: After Tito, ethnic tensions rose → Slobodan Milošević’s Serbian nationalism → Slovenia, Croatia, and Bosnia declared independence → ethnic cleansing in the Bosnian war and the Srebrenica massacre (1995, about 8,000 Muslim men and boys) → the Dayton Accords; in 1999 NATO bombed Serbia over Kosovo.

detail.zh: 国际刑事法庭(ICTY)审判 Milošević 等人。说明民族主义在冷战后欧洲依然致命。
detail.en: The ICTY tried Milošević and others. It showed that nationalism remained lethal in post–Cold War Europe.

summary.en: Northern Ireland’s "Troubles" (Catholic nationalists vs. Protestant unionists, the IRA) → the Good Friday Agreement (1998); Spain’s Basque separatist group ETA; independence referendums in Catalonia and Scotland — Western Europe mostly handled these peacefully and constitutionally.

detail.zh: 对比:东欧/巴尔干民族冲突更暴力,西欧多以权力下放(devolution)缓解。比利时 Flemish 与 Walloons 的语言分歧导致联邦化。
detail.en: Contrast: Balkan conflicts were far more violent, while Western Europe eased tensions through devolution. Belgium’s Flemish–Walloon language divide led to federalization.

summary.zh: 二战削弱欧洲 + 民族主义运动 + 美苏反对旧殖民主义 → India 独立(1947,Gandhi 非暴力,分治致大规模暴力)→ Algerian War(1954–1962,法国的血腥战争,导致第四共和国垮台)→ 1960 "非洲年"。
summary.en: WWII weakened Europe + nationalist movements + U.S. and Soviet opposition to old colonialism → Indian independence (1947, Gandhi’s nonviolence; partition brought mass violence) → the Algerian War (1954–1962), a brutal French war that toppled the Fourth Republic → Africa’s "Year of Africa" (1960).

detail.zh: Suez Crisis(1956):英法以失败告终,标志欧洲帝国时代结束。Vietnam(Dien Bien Phu 1954)。葡萄牙最晚(1970 年代)。亚洲领袖:Ho Chi Minh(Viet Minh 抗法)、Sukarno(Indonesia 抗荷);许多新国家加入 Non-Aligned Movement。
detail.en: The Suez Crisis (1956) ended in British and French humiliation, marking the end of the imperial age. Vietnam (Dien Bien Phu, 1954). Portugal let go last (1970s). Asian leaders: Ho Chi Minh (the Viet Minh against France) and Sukarno (Indonesia against the Dutch); many new states joined the Non-Aligned Movement.

summary.zh: 战后劳动力短缺 → guest workers(西德的土耳其劳工)和前殖民地移民(英国的 Windrush 一代、法国的北非人)→ 多元文化社会;同时出现反移民与右翼民粹政党(National Front)、关于伊斯兰与世俗的争论(头巾禁令)。
summary.en: Postwar labor shortages → guest workers (Turks in West Germany) and migrants from former colonies (Britain’s Windrush generation, North Africans in France) → multicultural societies; also anti-immigrant movements and right-wing populist parties (the National Front) and debates over Islam and secularism (headscarf bans).

detail.zh: 2015 年叙利亚等地难民危机,Merkel 接收约 100 万人,引发欧盟内部分歧,也是 Brexit 背景之一。
detail.en: The 2015 refugee crisis (Syria and beyond): Merkel admitted about a million people, dividing the EU and feeding into Brexit.

summary.en: Nuclear power and weapons, the space race (Sputnik, 1957), the Green Revolution and medical advances (antibiotics, vaccines, the pill), computers and the internet (Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web at CERN, 1989–1991) → higher living standards and life expectancy.

detail.zh: 负面:Chernobyl(1986)核事故、环境污染 → 环保运动。
detail.en: Downsides: the Chernobyl disaster (1986) and pollution → the environmental movement.

summary.en: Trade liberalization (WTO), multinationals, capital flows, the internet → deeper economic interdependence; the 2008 global financial crisis → the eurozone debt crisis in Greece and elsewhere, with austerity; anti-globalization and populism grew.

detail.en: Climate change, terrorism (Madrid 2004, London 2005, Paris 2015), and COVID-19 required international cooperation. International institutions: the IMF, World Bank, and GATT → WTO.

summary.zh: Existentialism(Sartre、Camus):在无意义的世界中自己赋予意义;postmodernism;美国流行文化("美国化");世俗化:教堂出席率下降;Vatican II(1962–1965)现代化天主教;低生育率与人口老龄化。
summary.en: Existentialism (Sartre, Camus): people create meaning in a meaningless world; postmodernism; American popular culture ("Americanization"); secularization: falling church attendance; Vatican II (1962–1965) modernized Catholicism; low fertility and aging populations.

detail.zh: 人口老龄化给养老金和福利国家带来压力,也使欧洲依赖移民劳动力。宗教人物:反纳粹的 Dietrich Bonhoeffer、Martin Niemöller;Pope John XXIII 召开 Vatican II。一些国家推出鼓励生育(pronatalist)政策;基因工程引发伦理争论。
detail.en: Aging strains pensions and welfare states and makes Europe reliant on immigrant labor. Religious figures: anti-Nazi pastors Dietrich Bonhoeffer and Martin Niemöller; Pope John XXIII convened Vatican II. Some states adopted pronatalist policies; genetic engineering raised ethical debates.

summary.en: Modernism: literature — Kafka, Joyce, Virginia Woolf (stream of consciousness, alienation); art — Cubism, Futurism, Dada, Surrealism, the Bauhaus, and after 1945 Abstract Expressionism and Pop Art; music — Stravinsky, Schoenberg (atonality).

detail.zh: 共同点:打破传统形式、表达战争与工业社会带来的不确定与异化;战后美国(纽约)取代巴黎成为艺术中心,大众消费文化兴起。
detail.en: Common thread: breaking traditional forms to express the uncertainty and alienation of war and industrial society; after 1945 New York replaced Paris as the art capital, and consumer culture boomed.
